## Overview

This report contains the preregistered eye-tracking and final test analyses from the OSF
preregistration
([osf.io/8env4](https://osf.io/8env4/overview)), *Prequestions and Attention: An
Eye-tracking Study*.

**Design.** Mixed design.

- **Between subjects, `Condition`:** Control (no prequestions), Polio prequestions, TB
  prequestions.
- **Within subjects, `Topic`:** sentences containing Polio-prequestioned information vs.
  TB-prequestioned information. Sentences unrelated to either set of prequestions are not
  analysed.

**Prediction.** Readers given Polio prequestions should process Polio sentences more than
TB sentences, readers given TB prequestions should show the reverse, and Control readers
should show no difference.

**DVs** (one per sentence and participant), grouped into global and local measures:

*Global (late) measures* reflect all processing of the sentence, including returns to it:

1. **Total gaze duration:** the summed duration of all fixations on the sentence.
2. **Re-reading (second-pass) time:** time on the sentence outside the first pass, i.e.
   returns to it after first-pass reading (total gaze − first-pass duration; with the
   derived measures also excluding the brief landing glances before reading reached the
   sentence). This operationalises the preregistered re-reading measure (see the
   deviation note below).

*Local (early) measures* reflect processing on first encounter with the sentence:

3. **First-pass duration:** the summed duration of fixations from first entering the
   sentence until first leaving it (only for sentences read during first-pass reading).
4. **First-pass regression** (0/1): after reading the sentence for the first time, did
   the reader leave it **backwards** (to an earlier sentence; = 1) or **forwards** (on to
   the next sentence; = 0)? Only the direction in which the eyes first leave the
   sentence counts; looking back *within* the sentence does not. Defined only for
   sentences read during first-pass reading, and not for the first sentence on a page
   (there is no earlier text to go back to).

An additional, non-preregistered global measure, **second-pass regressions** (returns
to the sentence from later text), is analysed in its own section.

**Source of the measures.** This version of the report uses the
**`r if (params$measures == "derived") "measures derived from the fixation data" else "measures exported by Tobii Pro Lab"`**
(`params$measures = "`r params$measures`"`).
`r if (params$measures == "derived") "The same report rendered with Tobii's own metrics is the sensitivity analysis (preq_eyetracking_analysis_tobii.html)." else "This is the sensitivity analysis; the main report uses measures derived from the fixation data (preq_eyetracking_analysis.html)."`

::: callout-important
## Deviation: measures derived from fixation data

Tobii Pro Lab's sentence metrics have two problems in this data set, so the main
analysis recomputes the measures from the fixation-level export
(`derive_et_measures.R`, which documents every step):

1. **Page landing.** When a page appears, readers' eyes usually land partway down it and
   then move to the first line. Tobii treats the sentences above the landing point as
   already passed and records their first-pass time as 0 (for about 84% of first
   sentences on a page). The derived measures start reading on each page at the first
   fixation on its first sentence.
2. **Vertical drift.** Recorded gaze is often offset by up to about half a line, so Tobii
   sometimes labels a fixation with the sentence on the neighbouring line. The derived
   measures assign fixations to text lines using runs of fixations along a line and a
   per-reader drift correction, limited to the 0.5° calibration accuracy that every
   included recording met (about 0.45 of a line on this setup: 24-inch monitor, 65 cm,
   no chin rest). Drift larger than that, which can build up through head movement, is
   not corrected.

Total gaze duration changes little (it does not depend on where passes begin), while
first-pass and second-pass time change substantially. All analyses can be reproduced
with Tobii's metrics by rendering with `-P measures:tobii`.
:::

**Length standardisation (deviation).** Target sentences differ in length (4–39 words),
so with `length_norm = TRUE` all measures are expressed per word of the sentence
(ms/word). Set `length_norm <- FALSE` in Setup to reproduce the
analyses in raw units.

**Models.** No duration is analysed with a linear mixed model, because reading-time
distributions are strongly right-skewed. The preregistration specified an ex-Gaussian
model for skewed durations:

- **Total gaze duration:** the preregistered ex-Gaussian model (gamlss), focusing on μ
  and also reporting τ.
- **First-pass duration:** a Gamma GLMM (log link). The ex-Gaussian could not be
  estimated (σ collapsed to zero in both gamlss and brms): first-pass durations include
  a large cluster of very brief first passes, so there is no Gaussian component.
- **Re-reading (second-pass) time:** a hurdle (zero-inflated) Gamma model, because 37%
  of sentences were never re-read. It is fitted as its two independent parts: a logistic
  GLMM for *whether* a sentence was re-read and a Gamma GLMM for *how long* it was
  re-read when it was.
- **First-pass regression:** the preregistered logistic GLMM.

```r
gamlss(total ~ condition * topic + re(random = ~ 1 | participant),
       nu.formula = ~ condition * topic, family = exGAUS)
glmer(first_pass ~ condition * topic + (1 + topic | participant), family = Gamma(link = "log"))
glmer(reread_any ~ condition * topic + (1 + topic | participant) + (1 | sentence),
      family = binomial)
glmer(reread_time ~ condition * topic + (1 + topic | participant), family = Gamma(link = "log"))
glmer(regression ~ condition * topic + (1 + topic | participant) + (1 | sentence),
      family = binomial)
```

All duration effects are reported on the original scale (ms per word): Gamma-model
contrasts are differences in model-predicted durations, not log-scale coefficients.

::: callout-important
## Deviation: operationalisation of re-reading

Tobii Pro Lab's `Re-reading_duration` is *go-past (regression-path) time minus first-pass
time*. Most of it is fixation time on **other, earlier sentences** after the reader leaves
the target, so it does not measure re-reading of the target sentence. Re-reading is therefore measured as **second-pass
time**: all fixations on the target sentence after first-pass reading, including returns
to it later.
:::

### Exclusions

Participants without eye-tracking data for all 4 text pages are excluded, because an
incomplete recording leaves them with an unbalanced set of Polio and TB sentences.
Participants in a prequestion condition without pretest data are also excluded, because
their prior knowledge cannot be assessed. Participants without final test data are
excluded so that every analysed participant has both eye-tracking and memory data.

```{r}
#| label: exclusions
# Exclusions are applied in R/data.R; shown here
kable(excluded_incomplete, col.names = c("Participant", "Condition", "N pages", "Pages recorded"),
      caption = "Excluded: eye-tracking data for fewer than all 4 pages")
kable(excluded_no_pretest, col.names = c("Participant", "Condition"),
      caption = "Excluded: prequestion condition but no pretest data")
kable(excluded_no_test, col.names = c("Participant", "Condition"),
      caption = "Excluded: no final test data")
kable(excluded_calibration, digits = 2,
      col.names = c("Participant", "Condition", "Accuracy (°)", "Precision (°)"),
      caption = "Excluded: calibration worse than the preregistered 0.5° criterion")
kable(n_by_cond, col.names = c("Condition", "N participants"),
      caption = "Participants per condition after exclusions")
```

### Calibration

Calibration was validated in Tobii Pro Lab before reading. Accuracy and precision (SD of
gaze samples), in degrees of visual angle, come from the lab run sheet
(`data/raw/calibration/et_run_sheet.tsv`; participant names removed, see the README there).

```{r}
#| label: calibration
# Calibration of the analysed participants (computed in R/data.R)
calib_summary |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = c("Measure", ".value"), names_sep = "_") |>
  kable(digits = 2, caption = sprintf(
    "Calibration validation (degrees), %d of %d analysed participants with data",
    calib_n, nlevels(dat$participant)))
kable(calib_by_cond, digits = 2, caption = "Calibration validation by condition (degrees)")
kable(select(calib_missing, participant, condition),
      caption = "Analysed participants without calibration data")
```

::: callout-note
The preregistration also excludes participants with calibration accuracy or precision
worse than **0.5°**. Participants worse than this on accuracy or precision are excluded
(see Exclusions); participants without calibration data in the run sheet are kept,
because the criterion cannot be checked for them. The preregistered exclusion for high **prior
knowledge** is not yet applied; add those IDs to `excluded_prereg` above once the
information is available.
:::

### Fixations and sentence regions

`r if (params$measures != "derived") "These figures show the sentence regions and fixation processing used for the derived measures (main report); this sensitivity version uses Tobii's own areas of interest."`

Each target sentence is an area of interest (AOI). Because sentences wrap across lines,
a sentence's AOI is made of one rectangle per line it occupies. @fig-aois shows these
regions on the four pages, as rebuilt from the page layout by `derive_et_measures.R`.
@fig-scanpath shows how one reader's fixations on one page are assigned to sentences
after drift correction.

```{r}
#| label: fig-aois
#| fig-cap: "The four text pages with the sentence regions (areas of interest) used for the derived measures. Each sentence is one region, made of one rectangle per text line. Polio target sentences are blue, TB target sentences orange, and other (filler) sentences grey; numbers give each sentence's order on the page."
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 7.4
regions <- read_tsv("data/derived/sentence_regions.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(role = factor(case_when(type == "PO" ~ "Polio target", type == "TB" ~ "TB target",
                                 TRUE ~ "Other sentence"),
                       levels = c("Polio target", "TB target", "Other sentence")))
role_cols <- c(`Polio target` = unname(topic_cols["Polio"]),
               `TB target` = unname(topic_cols["TB"]), `Other sentence` = "grey45")

# label each sentence once, at the start of its first line
region_labels <- regions |>
  group_by(page, sentence_index) |>
  slice_min(line, n = 1) |>
  ungroup()

# label_size: size of the sentence-number labels (mm)
page_panel <- function(p, title = sprintf("Page %d", p), label_size = 2.6) {
  img <- png::readPNG(sprintf("stimuli/pages/page%d_full.png", p))
  r <- filter(regions, page == p)
  ggplot(r) +
    annotation_raster(img, 0, 1, 0, 1) +
    geom_rect(aes(xmin = x0, xmax = x1, ymin = 1 - y1, ymax = 1 - y0, colour = role,
                  fill = role), alpha = 0.12, linewidth = 0.35) +
    geom_label(data = filter(region_labels, page == p),
               aes(x = x0, y = 1 - (y0 + y1) / 2, label = sentence_index, colour = role),
               size = label_size, fontface = "bold", label.padding = unit(0.08, "lines"),
               hjust = 1.1,
               show.legend = FALSE) +
    # one legend (fill), shared by all four panels
    scale_colour_manual(values = role_cols, guide = "none", drop = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = role_cols, name = NULL, drop = FALSE,
                      guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 0.35,
                                                               colour = role_cols))) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-0.02, 1), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    coord_fixed(9 / 16) +
    labs(title = title) +
    theme_void(base_size = 11) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")) +
    # only page 2 contains all three sentence types, so only its legend is kept
    (if (p == 2) NULL else guides(fill = "none"))
}

wrap_plots(map(1:4, page_panel), ncol = 2, guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Models

Durations are fitted with Gamma GLMMs (`glmmTMB`, log link) and binary measures with
`glmer` (binomial, logit link).

**Random-effects selection.** Every GLMM starts from the maximal random-effects
structure the design allows (Barr et al., 2013): random intercepts for participants and
sentences, by-participant slopes for every effect that varies within participants
(Topic; or prequestioned vs. non-prequestioned), and by-sentence slopes for every effect
that varies within sentences (Condition, because each sentence is read in all three
conditions; or prequestioned vs. non-prequestioned). The structure is then reduced by
model comparison (Matuschek et al., 2017):

1. If the maximal model is singular or does not converge
   (`performance::check_singularity()`, `performance::check_convergence()`), the
   random-effect correlations are removed.
2. Backward selection of random slopes: each remaining slope is removed in turn, and the
   reduced model is compared with the current one by a likelihood-ratio test. The slope
   whose removal worsens the fit least is dropped if *p* > .20 (the criterion
   recommended by Matuschek et al., 2017), or if the current model is still singular.
   This is repeated until every remaining slope improves the fit (*p* ≤ .20).

Condition's two codes (Polio vs. Control, TB vs. Control) are treated as one slope. The
random intercepts are always kept. All comparisons are listed in the
[random-effects selection table](#sec-re-selection).

```{r}
#| label: fit-models
# ---- Random-effects selection (see text above) ----------------------------------------
# A random-effects structure is a list: grouping factor -> named list of slopes, where
# each slope is a character vector of numeric predictor codes (Condition has two).
# Maximal structure for the Condition x Topic design:
re_max_ct <- list(participant = list(Topic = "topic_c"),
                  sentence    = list(Condition = c("cond_polio", "cond_tb")))

fit_prereg <- function(dv, family) {
  d <- droplevels(dat[!is.na(dat[[dv]]), ])
  fit_glmm(paste(dv, "~ condition * topic"), d, family, re_max_ct)
}

models <- dvs |>
  mutate(model   = map2(dv, family, fit_prereg),
         re_used = map_chr(model, ~ attr(.x, "re_used")))

models |>
  transmute(DV = label,
            `Random effects retained` = re_used,
            `N obs` = map_int(model, nobs),
            `R² (marginal)` = map_dbl(model, ~ tryCatch(r2(.x)$R2_marginal, error = \(e) NA_real_)),
            `R² (conditional)` = map_dbl(model, ~ tryCatch(r2(.x)$R2_conditional, error = \(e) NA_real_))) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Fitted models (Nakagawa's R², on the latent scale for the GLMMs)")

```

### Omnibus tests

```{r}
#| label: omnibus
anova_tab <- models |>
  mutate(tab = map2(model, family, omnibus)) |>
  select(dv, label, tab) |>
  unnest(tab)

anova_tab |>
  transmute(DV = label, Effect = Parameter,
            Test = if_else(test == "F", "F", "Wald χ²"),
            Statistic = stat,
            df = if_else(test == "F", sprintf("%d, %.1f", df, df_error), as.character(df)),
            p = format_p(p, name = NULL, digits = 3)) |>
  kable(digits = 2, caption = "Type-III omnibus tests")
```

### Topic effect within each condition

The contrasts are Polio − TB within each condition, estimated with
`modelbased::estimate_contrasts()`. For the durations, the preregistered predictions are
directional: a **positive** difference in the Polio condition and a **negative**
difference in the TB condition. These contrasts are tested **one-sided** in the
predicted direction. The prediction for Control is *no difference*, so that contrast is
tested two-sided. The preregistration gives no direction for first-pass regressions, so
all of its contrasts are two-sided; they are differences in the probability of a
regression (percentage points, *z* tests). Confidence intervals are the usual two-sided
95% intervals.

```{r}
#| label: contrasts
# One-sided p-values in the preregistered direction (Polio − TB):
#   Polio condition: > 0; TB condition: < 0; Control: two-sided (null prediction)
predicted <- c(Control = "two-sided", Polio = "greater", TB = "less")

add_directional <- function(x) {
  x |>
    mutate(t = if ("t" %in% names(x)) t else NA_real_,
           z = if ("z" %in% names(x)) z else NA_real_,
           stat_name = if_else(is.na(t), "z", "t"),
           stat = coalesce(t, z),
           df = if ("df" %in% names(x)) coalesce(df, Inf) else Inf,
           prediction = if_else(directional, predicted[as.character(condition)], "two-sided"),
           p_test = case_when(
             prediction == "greater" ~ pt(stat, df, lower.tail = FALSE),
             prediction == "less"    ~ pt(stat, df, lower.tail = TRUE),
             TRUE                    ~ p),
           p_type = if_else(prediction == "two-sided", "two-sided", "one-sided"))
}

contrast_tab <- models |>
  mutate(tab = map(model, \(m) est_contrasts(m, contrast = "topic", by = "condition",
                                             comparison = "revpairwise") |>
                     as.data.frame() |>
                     add_satterthwaite(m, focal = "topic", by = "condition"))) |>
  select(dv, label, unit, directional, tab) |>
  unnest(tab) |>
  # LMMs: t with Satterthwaite df; the logistic GLMM: z on the probability scale
  # (df = Inf, so pt() = pnorm())
  add_directional() |>
  # probabilities -> percentage points
  mutate(across(c(Difference, SE, CI_low, CI_high), \(x) if_else(unit == "%", 100 * x, x)))

contrast_tab |>
  transmute(DV = label, Condition = condition,
            Contrast = paste(Level1, "−", Level2),
            Difference, SE,
            `95% CI` = fmt_ci(CI_low, CI_high, 1),
            Test = stat_name, Statistic = stat,
            df = if_else(is.infinite(df), "—", as.character(df)),
            Prediction = case_when(!directional ~ "none (two-sided)",
                                   prediction == "greater" ~ "Polio > TB",
                                   prediction == "less" ~ "Polio < TB",
                                   TRUE ~ "no difference"),
            p = format_p(p_test, name = NULL, digits = 3),
            `p type` = p_type) |>
  kable(digits = 2, caption = "Topic contrasts within each condition (durations in ms/word or ms, first-pass regression in percentage points; p uncorrected; one-sided in the predicted direction where a direction was preregistered)")
```

```{r}
#| label: means
means_tab <- models |>
  mutate(tab = map(model, ~ est_means(.x, by = c("condition", "topic")) |>
                     as.data.frame() |>
                     # modelbased calls the estimate "Probability" for logistic models
                     rename(any_of(c(Mean = "Probability"))))) |>
  select(dv, label, unit, tab) |>
  unnest(tab) |>
  # probabilities -> percent
  mutate(across(c(Mean, SE, CI_low, CI_high), \(x) if_else(unit == "%", 100 * x, x)))
```

### Main effects and interaction contrasts

The omnibus tests show *whether* there is a main effect or interaction. These contrasts
show *where*, for every measure:

- **Condition main effect:** pairwise differences between conditions, averaged over
  topic (Polio − Control, TB − Control, TB − Polio).
- **Topic main effect:** Polio − TB sentences, averaged over the three conditions.
- **Interaction contrasts:** whether the topic effect (Polio − TB) differs between two
  conditions, e.g. (Polio − TB in the Polio condition) − (Polio − TB in Control).

All are computed from predictions averaged over the observed sample within each
Condition × Topic cell (`marginaleffects::avg_predictions()`, matching
`estimate = "average"` above), so cells are weighted equally and each cell mean
reflects its participants' random effects. Gamma-model contrasts are in ms per word and
logistic-model contrasts are differences in probability (percentage points); all use *z*
tests. All are two-sided. The three
condition comparisons and the three interaction contrasts are each Holm-adjusted as a
family; confidence intervals are unadjusted. For the logistic models, the omnibus Wald
tests are on the log-odds scale while these contrasts are on the probability scale, so
the two can disagree (an interaction can be reliable in log-odds without any single
probability contrast surviving the correction).

```{r}
#| label: followups
# The six Condition x Topic cells, in this fixed order:
#   Control-Polio, Control-TB, Polio-Polio, Polio-TB, TB-Polio, TB-TB
cell_grid <- function(m) {
  mf <- model.frame(m)
  expand_grid(condition = factor(levels(mf$condition), levels(mf$condition)),
              topic = factor(levels(mf$topic), levels(mf$topic)))
}

# Each contrast is a set of weights over the six cells
followup_weights <- list(
  `Condition: Polio − Control`        = c(-.5, -.5, .5, .5, 0, 0),
  `Condition: TB − Control`           = c(-.5, -.5, 0, 0, .5, .5),
  `Condition: TB − Polio`             = c(0, 0, -.5, -.5, .5, .5),
  `Topic: Polio − TB`                 = c(1, -1, 1, -1, 1, -1) / 3,
  `Interaction: Polio vs. Control`    = c(-1, 1, 1, -1, 0, 0),
  `Interaction: TB vs. Control`       = c(-1, 1, 0, 0, 1, -1),
  `Interaction: Polio vs. TB`         = c(0, 0, 1, -1, -1, 1)
)

followups <- function(m, unit) {
  g <- cell_grid(m)
  H <- do.call(cbind, followup_weights)
  # cell means: predictions for every observation, averaged within each cell
  cells <- as.data.frame(marginaleffects::avg_predictions(m, by = c("condition", "topic"),
                                                          type = "response"))
  stopifnot(identical(as.character(cells$condition), as.character(g$condition)),
            identical(as.character(cells$topic), as.character(g$topic)))
  pr <- as.data.frame(marginaleffects::avg_predictions(m, by = c("condition", "topic"),
                                                       type = "response", hypothesis = H))
  out <- tibble(effect = names(followup_weights), estimate = pr$estimate,
                se = pr$std.error, stat = pr$statistic, df = Inf, p = pr$p.value)
  if (inherits(m, "lmerModLmerTest")) {
    # Satterthwaite df: rebuild each contrast as weights on the fixed effects
    fixed_terms <- delete.response(terms(reformulas::nobars(formula(m))))
    X <- model.matrix(fixed_terms, g, contrasts.arg = attr(model.matrix(m), "contrasts"))
    # Satterthwaite df of the corresponding fixed-effects contrast (approximation)
    ct <- lmerTest::contest(m, t(H) %*% X, joint = FALSE, ddf = "Satterthwaite")
    gap <- max(abs(ct$Estimate - out$estimate) / out$se)
    if (gap > 0.1) warning(sprintf("Averaged and fixed-effects follow-up contrasts differ by up to %.2f SE; Satterthwaite df are approximate.", gap))
    out <- mutate(out, df = ct$df, p = 2 * pt(-abs(stat), df))
  }
  crit <- if_else(is.infinite(out$df), qnorm(0.975), qt(0.975, out$df))
  out <- out |>
    mutate(lo = estimate - crit * se, hi = estimate + crit * se,
           family = str_extract(effect, "^[A-Za-z]+"),
           test = if_else(is.infinite(df), "z", "t"))
  if (unit == "%") out <- mutate(out, across(c(estimate, se, lo, hi), \(x) 100 * x))
  out |>
    group_by(family) |>
    mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p, method = "holm")) |>
    ungroup()
}

followup_tab <- models |>
  mutate(tab = map2(model, unit, followups)) |>
  select(dv, label, level, unit, tab) |>
  unnest(tab)

followup_tab |>
  transmute(Level = level, DV = label, Effect = effect,
            Estimate = fmt_num(estimate, 1),
            `95% CI` = fmt_ci(lo, hi, 1),
            Test = test, Statistic = fmt_num(stat, 2),
            df = if_else(is.infinite(df), "—", fmt_num(df, 0)),
            p = format_p(p, name = NULL, digits = 3),
            `p (Holm)` = format_p(p_adj, name = NULL, digits = 3)) |>
  kable(caption = "Main-effect and interaction contrasts for each measure (durations in ms/word or ms; first-pass regression in percentage points). Interaction contrasts are differences in the Polio − TB effect between two conditions.")
```

## Figures

```{r}
#| label: fig-observed
#| fig-cap: "Observed data. Thin grey lines connect each participant's Polio and TB sentence means. Large points are condition means ± 95% CI computed across participants."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 14
subj_means <- dat |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(dvs$dv), names_to = "dv", values_to = "value") |>
  group_by(participant, condition, topic, dv) |>
  summarise(value = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(!is.nan(value)) |>                       # no first pass on any such sentence
  # first-pass regression: proportion of sentences -> percent
  mutate(value = if_else(dv %in% dvs$dv[dvs$unit == "%"], 100 * value, value))

plot_observed <- function(dv_name) {
  meta <- filter(dvs, dv == dv_name)
  dd <- filter(subj_means, dv == dv_name)
  summ <- dd |>
    group_by(condition, topic) |>
    summarise(m = mean(value), se = sd(value) / sqrt(n()), .groups = "drop")
  ggplot(dd, aes(topic, value)) +
    geom_line(aes(group = participant), colour = "grey75", linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = topic), size = 1.2, alpha = 0.35,
               position = position_jitter(width = 0.04, height = 0, seed = 1)) +
    geom_line(data = summ, aes(y = m, group = 1), linewidth = 1, colour = "grey20") +
    geom_errorbar(data = summ, aes(y = m, ymin = m - 1.96 * se, ymax = m + 1.96 * se),
                  width = 0.08, linewidth = 0.8, colour = "grey20") +
    geom_point(data = summ, aes(y = m, fill = topic), shape = 21, size = 3.5,
               colour = "white", stroke = 1) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = topic_cols, guide = "none") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = topic_cols, guide = "none") +
    facet_wrap(~ condition) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = meta$unit, title = meta$label)
}

wrap_plots(map(dvs$dv, plot_observed), ncol = 1) +
  plot_annotation(caption = "Sentence topic")
```

## Results

```{r}
#| label: writeup-helpers
# Omnibus test for one DV and term:
#   LMM:  "*F*(2, 140.6) = 3.87, *p* = .021"
#   GLMM: "χ²(2) = 15.28, *p* < .001"
F_txt <- function(dv_name, term) {
  r <- filter(anova_tab, dv == dv_name, Parameter == term)
  p_txt <- sub("^p", "*p*", apa_p(r$p))
  if (r$test == "F") {
    sprintf("*F*(%d, %.1f) = %s, %s", r$df, r$df_error, apa_num(r$stat), p_txt)
  } else {
    sprintf("χ²(%d) = %s, %s", r$df, apa_num(r$stat), p_txt)
  }
}
sig <- function(dv_name, term) filter(anova_tab, dv == dv_name, Parameter == term)$p < .05

# Within-condition topic contrast, e.g. "*b* = 696 ms, 95% CI [208, 1185], *t*(1403) = 2.79, *p* = .005"
C_txt <- function(dv_name, cond) {
  r <- filter(contrast_tab, dv == dv_name, condition == cond)
  d <- switch(r$unit, ms = 0, `ms/word` = 1, `%` = 1, 2)
  unit_txt <- if (r$unit == "%") "percentage points" else r$unit
  stat_txt <- if (r$stat_name == "z") sprintf("*z* = %s", apa_num(r$stat)) else
    sprintf("*t*(%.0f) = %s", r$df, apa_num(r$stat))
  one <- r$p_type == "one-sided"
  sprintf("%s = %s %s, %s, %s, %s",
          if (r$unit == "%") "Δ" else "*b*",
          apa_num(r$Difference, d), unit_txt,
          ci_part(r$Difference, r$SE, r$CI_low, r$CI_high, one, r$df, d),
          stat_txt, p_part(r$p_test, r$stat, r$df, one))
}

# Follow-up contrasts for one measure, as one sentence (Holm-adjusted p)
FU_txt <- function(tab) {
  unit_txt <- if (tab$unit[1] == "%") " pp" else paste0(" ", tab$unit[1])
  one <- function(eff) {
    r <- filter(tab, effect == eff)
    stopifnot(nrow(r) == 1)
    sprintf("%s%s [%s, %s], %s", fmt_num(r$estimate, 1), unit_txt, fmt_num(r$lo, 1),
            fmt_num(r$hi, 1), sub("^p", "*p*", apa_p(if (r$family == "Topic") r$p else r$p_adj)))
  }
  sprintf(paste0(
    "Averaged over topic, the conditions differed by %s (Polio − Control), %s (TB − Control)",
    " and %s (TB − Polio); averaged over conditions, Polio − TB sentences differed by %s.",
    " The topic effect (Polio − TB) differed between the Polio condition and Control by %s,",
    " between the TB condition and Control by %s, and between the Polio and TB conditions",
    " by %s (interaction contrasts; condition and interaction contrasts Holm-adjusted)."),
    one("Condition: Polio − Control"), one("Condition: TB − Control"),
    one("Condition: TB − Polio"), one("Topic: Polio − TB"),
    one("Interaction: Polio vs. Control"), one("Interaction: TB vs. Control"),
    one("Interaction: Polio vs. TB"))
}
FU <- function(dv_name) FU_txt(filter(followup_tab, dv == dv_name))

# Model-estimated mean for one DV x condition x topic, e.g. "48.2%"
M_txt <- function(dv_name, cond, tp) {
  r <- filter(means_tab, dv == dv_name, condition == cond, topic == tp)
  stopifnot(nrow(r) == 1)
  sprintf("%s%s", fmt_num(r$Mean, 1), if (r$unit == "%") "%" else paste0(" ", r$unit))
}
C_sig <- function(dv_name, cond) filter(contrast_tab, dv == dv_name, condition == cond)$p_test < .05

# Sentence describing both main effects, worded according to which are significant
main_txt <- function(dv_name) {
  fc <- F_txt(dv_name, "condition"); ft <- F_txt(dv_name, "topic")
  sc <- sig(dv_name, "condition");   st <- sig(dv_name, "topic")
  if (!sc && !st) {
    sprintf("Neither the main effect of Condition, %s, nor the main effect of Topic, %s, was significant.", fc, ft)
  } else if (sc && st) {
    sprintf("Both the main effect of Condition, %s, and the main effect of Topic, %s, were significant.", fc, ft)
  } else {
    sprintf("The main effect of Condition was %s, %s, and the main effect of Topic was %s, %s.",
            yn(sc), fc, yn(st), ft)
  }
}

# Sentence describing the random-effects structure retained
re_used <- set_names(models$re_used, models$label)
re_sentence <- paste0(
  "Random effects were selected from the maximal structure (by-participant intercepts and Topic slopes; by-sentence intercepts and Condition slopes) by likelihood-ratio tests (see Models). The final structures were: ",
  paste(sprintf("%s, %s", tolower(names(re_used)), re_used), collapse = "; "), ".")
```

`r excl_txt(excluded_incomplete, "had eye-tracking data for fewer than all 4 text pages")`
`r excl_txt(excluded_no_pretest, "were in a prequestion condition but had no pretest data")`
`r excl_txt(excluded_no_test, "had no final test data")`
`r excl_txt(excluded_calibration, "had calibration accuracy or precision worse than 0.5°")` The analyses included `r n_total`
participants (Control: `r n_by_cond$n[1]`, Polio: `r n_by_cond$n[2]`, TB:
`r n_by_cond$n[3]`). Each read 5 Polio-relevant and 5 TB-relevant sentences.
`r n_missing` sentence observations had no eye-tracking data and were excluded.
First-pass duration and first-pass regression are defined only for sentences read during
first-pass reading, and first-pass regression not for the first sentence on a page,
where there is no earlier text to regress to
(`r sum(!is.na(dat$first_pass))` and `r sum(!is.na(dat$fp_regression))` observations).
First-pass duration and re-reading duration (for re-read sentences) were analysed with
Gamma GLMMs (log link), and first-pass regression and whether a sentence was re-read with
logistic GLMMs that also included a random intercept for sentence. Total gaze duration
was analysed with the preregistered ex-Gaussian model (separate section). All models included Condition (Control, Polio, TB;
between subjects), Topic (Polio, TB; within subjects), and their interaction as
effect-coded fixed effects. `r re_sentence` Omnibus effects were tested with type-III
Wald χ² tests. Topic contrasts (Polio − TB) within each
condition were estimated with `modelbased`. Following the preregistered directional
predictions, the duration contrasts in the Polio (Polio > TB) and TB (Polio < TB)
conditions were tested one-tailed. The Control contrasts, for which no difference was
predicted, and all first-pass regression contrasts, for which no direction was
preregistered, were tested two-tailed. First-pass regression contrasts are differences
in the probability of a regression, in percentage points; Gamma-model contrasts are
differences in model-predicted duration, in ms per word. For one-tailed tests, confidence
intervals are 90% intervals (matching a one-tailed test at α = .05) and the two-tailed *p*
value is given as well; otherwise they are 95% intervals. Means and contrasts were computed by averaging model
predictions over the observed sample (`modelbased` with the `marginaleffects` backend and
`estimate = "average"`), which incorporates the random-effect variation. All contrasts
are *z* tests.

### Global measures

**Total gaze duration** was analysed with the preregistered ex-Gaussian model; see
[the ex-Gaussian section](#sec-exgauss).

**Re-reading (second-pass) time** was analysed as a hurdle model with two parts.
*Whether* a sentence was re-read: the Condition × Topic interaction was
`r yn(sig("reread_any", "condition:topic"))`,
`r F_txt("reread_any", "condition:topic")`. `r main_txt("reread_any")` The Polio − TB
difference in the probability of re-reading was `r yn(C_sig("reread_any", "Polio"))` in
the Polio condition, `r C_txt("reread_any", "Polio")`; `r yn(C_sig("reread_any", "TB"))`
in the TB condition, `r C_txt("reread_any", "TB")`; and
`r yn(C_sig("reread_any", "Control"))` in the Control condition,
`r C_txt("reread_any", "Control")`. `r FU("reread_any")` *How long* re-read sentences
were re-read: the Condition × Topic interaction was
`r yn(sig("reread_time", "condition:topic"))`, `r F_txt("reread_time", "condition:topic")`.
`r main_txt("reread_time")` The Polio − TB difference was
`r yn(C_sig("reread_time", "Polio"))` in the Polio condition,
`r C_txt("reread_time", "Polio")`; `r yn(C_sig("reread_time", "TB"))` in the TB
condition, `r C_txt("reread_time", "TB")`; and `r yn(C_sig("reread_time", "Control"))`
in the Control condition, `r C_txt("reread_time", "Control")`. `r FU("reread_time")`

### Local measures

**First-pass duration.** The Condition × Topic interaction was
`r yn(sig("first_pass", "condition:topic"))`,
`r F_txt("first_pass", "condition:topic")`. `r main_txt("first_pass")` The Polio − TB
difference was `r yn(C_sig("first_pass", "Polio"))` in the Polio condition,
`r C_txt("first_pass", "Polio")`; `r yn(C_sig("first_pass", "TB"))` in the TB
condition, `r C_txt("first_pass", "TB")`; and `r yn(C_sig("first_pass", "Control"))`
in the Control condition, `r C_txt("first_pass", "Control")`. `r FU("first_pass")`

**First-pass regression.** Readers regressed out of
`r fmt_num(100 * mean(dat$fp_regression, na.rm = TRUE), 1)`% of the sentences they read
during first-pass reading. The Condition × Topic interaction was
`r yn(sig("fp_regression", "condition:topic"))`,
`r F_txt("fp_regression", "condition:topic")`. `r main_txt("fp_regression")` The
Polio − TB difference in the probability of a regression was
`r yn(C_sig("fp_regression", "Polio"))` in the Polio condition,
`r C_txt("fp_regression", "Polio")` (Polio sentences: `r M_txt("fp_regression", "Polio", "Polio")`;
TB sentences: `r M_txt("fp_regression", "Polio", "TB")`);
`r yn(C_sig("fp_regression", "TB"))` in the TB condition,
`r C_txt("fp_regression", "TB")` (`r M_txt("fp_regression", "TB", "Polio")` vs.
`r M_txt("fp_regression", "TB", "TB")`); and `r yn(C_sig("fp_regression", "Control"))`
in the Control condition, `r C_txt("fp_regression", "Control")`. `r FU("fp_regression")`
Topic is a property of the sentences (5 Polio and 5 TB sentences), and sentences differ
greatly in how often readers regress out of them (sentence random-intercept SD =
`r fmt_num(attr(VarCorr(models$model[[which(models$dv == "fp_regression")]])$sentence, "stddev"), 2)`
on the log-odds scale). With the preregistered sentence random intercept, each
within-condition topic contrast therefore carries this between-sentence uncertainty,
which makes its confidence interval wide. The Condition × Topic interaction compares the
same sentences across conditions and is the informative test of the prediction.

Observed data are shown in @fig-observed and model estimates in @fig-model.

## Total gaze duration: ex-Gaussian model (preregistered) {#sec-exgauss}

::: callout-note
## Preregistered model for skewed durations

The preregistration specified that heavily skewed durations would be analysed with an
ex-Gaussian distribution, focusing on μ. Total gaze duration is heavily skewed, so this
is its main analysis. The model also shows *how* prequestions change gaze duration: by
shifting typical reading time (μ), or by producing more very long readings (τ).
:::

Gaze durations are right-skewed. An ex-Gaussian distribution, a Gaussian component plus
an exponential tail, describes this shape with three parameters:

- **μ:** mean of the Gaussian component, the *typical* reading time;
- **σ:** spread of the Gaussian component;
- **τ:** mean of the exponential component, the size of the *slow tail*.

A prequestion effect on μ means prequestioned sentences are read uniformly longer. An
effect on τ means some prequestioned sentences are read much longer than usual.

The model is a distributional (GAMLSS) mixed model fitted with `gamlss` (`exGAUS`
family). gamlss parameterises the ex-Gaussian directly by μ, σ and τ (its `nu`
parameter, log link). μ and τ both depend on Condition × Topic (effect-coded), with
participant random intercepts on μ (`re()`, fitted by REML through `nlme`). σ is
constant. The overall mean is μ + τ.

Within each condition, the Polio − TB difference is computed for μ, τ and the mean.
Standard errors use the delta method on the fixed-effect covariance matrix, giving 95%
Wald CIs and two-sided *p*-values. gamlss estimates these standard errors conditional on
the random-effect estimates, so they may be slightly too small. Gaze duration is
modelled in units of `r if (length_norm) "100 ms/word" else "1 s"` and reported in
`r dur_unit`.

```{r}
#| label: exgauss-fit
library(gamlss)        # attaches nlme (masks only dplyr::collapse here)

ex_scale <- if (length_norm) 100 else 1000
ex_dat <- dat |>
  filter(!is.na(total_fix)) |>
  transmute(gaze = total_fix / ex_scale, condition, topic, participant) |>
  as.data.frame()                                    # gamlss refuses NA in any column

m_ex <- gamlss(gaze ~ condition * topic + re(random = ~ 1 | participant),
               sigma.formula = ~ 1, nu.formula = ~ condition * topic,
               family = exGAUS, data = ex_dat,
               control = gamlss.control(n.cyc = 200, trace = FALSE))
stopifnot(m_ex$converged)
```

```{r}
#| label: exgauss-contrasts
grid <- expand_grid(condition = factor(levels(ex_dat$condition), levels(ex_dat$condition)),
                    topic = factor(levels(ex_dat$topic), levels(ex_dat$topic)))
X <- model.matrix(~ condition * topic, grid)
b_mu <- coef(m_ex, "mu")[colnames(X)]
b_nu <- coef(m_ex, "nu")[colnames(X)]

# Fixed-effect covariance, ordered mu coefficients, sigma intercept, nu coefficients
V_ex <- suppressWarnings(vcov(m_ex, type = "vcov"))
k <- ncol(X)
stopifnot(nrow(V_ex) == 2 * k + 1)
pad <- \(g_mu, g_nu) c(g_mu, 0, g_nu)                # gradient over (mu, sigma, nu)

mu_cell  <- drop(X %*% b_mu)
tau_cell <- exp(drop(X %*% b_nu))
cell <- \(cnd, tp) which(grid$condition == cnd & grid$topic == tp)

ex_tab <- map(levels(ex_dat$condition), \(cnd) {
  i1 <- cell(cnd, "Polio"); i2 <- cell(cnd, "TB")
  d_mu  <- X[i1, ] - X[i2, ]
  d_tau <- tau_cell[i1] * X[i1, ] - tau_cell[i2] * X[i2, ]   # gradient of exp(.) difference
  est_mu <- sum(d_mu * b_mu); est_tau <- tau_cell[i1] - tau_cell[i2]
  tibble(parameter = c("Mean", "μ (Gaussian)", "τ (tail)"),
         est = c(est_mu + est_tau, est_mu, est_tau),
         se = map_dbl(list(pad(d_mu, d_tau), pad(d_mu, 0 * d_tau), pad(0 * d_mu, d_tau)),
                      \(g) sqrt(drop(t(g) %*% V_ex %*% g))))  |>
    mutate(condition = cnd)
}) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  mutate(across(c(est, se), \(x) x * ex_scale),
         lo = est - qnorm(0.975) * se, hi = est + qnorm(0.975) * se,
         p = 2 * pnorm(-abs(est / se)),
         parameter = factor(parameter, levels = c("Mean", "μ (Gaussian)", "τ (tail)")),
         condition = factor(condition, levels = levels(ex_dat$condition)))

ex_cells <- tibble(grid,
                   Mean = (mu_cell + tau_cell) * ex_scale,
                   `μ (Gaussian)` = mu_cell * ex_scale,
                   `τ (tail)` = tau_cell * ex_scale)

ex_cells |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) fmt_num(x, 1))) |>
  kable(caption = sprintf("Ex-Gaussian parameters by Condition × Topic (%s; fixed effects, average participant).",
                          dur_unit))

ex_tab |>
  transmute(Parameter = parameter, Condition = condition,
            `Polio − TB` = fmt_num(est, 1), SE = fmt_num(se, 1), `95% CI` = fmt_ci(lo, hi, 1),
            p = format_p(p, name = NULL)) |>
  kable(caption = sprintf("Polio − TB differences within each condition (%s). Delta-method SEs; two-sided p.",
                          dur_unit))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-exgauss
#| fig-cap: "Ex-Gaussian decomposition of the topic effect on total gaze duration. Points are estimated Polio − TB differences within each condition; bars are 95% confidence intervals. The prediction is positive in the Polio condition, negative in the TB condition, and about zero in Control."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 3.8
cond_cols3 <- c(Control = "#999999", topic_cols)

ggplot(ex_tab, aes(est, fct_rev(condition), colour = condition)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey70") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), linewidth = 0.9, size = 0.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cond_cols3, guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~ parameter, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = sprintf("Polio − TB difference (%s)", dur_unit), y = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: exgauss-writeup-helpers
E_row <- function(par, cnd) {
  r <- filter(ex_tab, parameter == par, condition == cnd)
  stopifnot(nrow(r) == 1)
  r
}
E_txt <- function(par, cnd) {
  r <- E_row(par, cnd)
  sprintf("%s %s, 95%% CI [%s, %s], %s", fmt_num(r$est, 1), dur_unit,
          fmt_num(r$lo, 1), fmt_num(r$hi, 1), format_p(r$p))
}
```

**Results.** The ex-Gaussian model converged after `r m_ex$iter` cycles. For the
**overall mean**, the Polio − TB difference was `r E_txt("Mean", "Polio")` in the Polio
condition, `r E_txt("Mean", "TB")` in the TB condition, and `r E_txt("Mean", "Control")`
in Control. For the **Gaussian component (μ)**, it was
`r E_txt("μ (Gaussian)", "Polio")` in the Polio condition,
`r E_txt("μ (Gaussian)", "TB")` in the TB condition, and
`r E_txt("μ (Gaussian)", "Control")` in Control. For the **exponential tail (τ)**, it
was `r E_txt("τ (tail)", "Polio")` in the Polio condition,
`r E_txt("τ (tail)", "TB")` in the TB condition, and `r E_txt("τ (tail)", "Control")`
in Control (@fig-exgauss).

## Prequestioned vs. non-prequestioned sentences

::: callout-note
## Preregistered hypothesis, different model

The preregistration predicts that "prequestioned information will result in longer gaze
durations and longer re-reading durations back to the prequestioned information compared
to non-prequestioned information." This section tests that hypothesis directly by pooling
the two prequestion conditions and comparing prequestioned with non-prequestioned
sentences.

The **hypothesis** is preregistered. The **model** here (relevance coding with a crossed
random effect for sentence) differs from the preregistered Condition × Topic model
above, so it should be reported as a deviation in model specification.
First-pass duration and first-pass regression are preregistered measures (analysis
plan). Comparing first-pass and second-pass time shows *when* any extra processing
happens: on first encounter (first pass) or on returning to the sentence (second pass).
:::

**Approach.** Only participants in the Polio and TB conditions are included, since Control
readers had no prequestioned sentences. Each target sentence is coded as
**Prequestioned** (its topic matches the reader's prequestions) or
**Non-prequestioned**. Every sentence is prequestioned for one condition and not for the
other, so the comparison is balanced over sentences. Relevance varies within
participants and within sentences, so the maximal model for each DV is:

```r
DV ~ relevance + (1 + relevance | participant) + (1 + relevance | sentence)
```

The by-sentence slope allows the effect of prequestioning to differ between sentences.
Durations use Gamma GLMMs (`glmmTMB`); binary measures use `glmer` (binomial, logit
link). Random effects are selected by the same model-comparison procedure as above.
Each contrast is Prequestioned − Non-prequestioned. Duration contrasts are tested
one-sided (Prequestioned > Non-prequestioned), following the preregistered hypothesis.
No direction was preregistered for first-pass regressions, so that contrast is
two-sided; it is a difference in the probability of a regression, in percentage points.
First-pass duration and first-pass regression are only analysed for sentences that were
read during first-pass reading.

```{r}
#| label: rel-models
# dat_rel (Polio and TB conditions, coded prequestioned / non-prequestioned) is built
# in R/data.R

# Total gaze duration is analysed with the ex-Gaussian model (below).
rel_dvs <- tribble(
  ~dv,             ~label,                                    ~level,   ~unit,     ~family,    ~directional,
  "reread_any",    "Re-reading: probability of re-reading",   "Global", "%",       "binomial", TRUE,
  "reread_time",   "Re-reading: duration when re-read",       "Global", dur_unit,  "gamma",    TRUE,
  "first_pass",    "First-pass duration",                     "Local",  dur_unit,  "gamma",    TRUE,
  "fp_regression", "First-pass regression",                   "Local",  "%",       "binomial", FALSE
)

# Maximal structure for the prequestioned vs. non-prequestioned design
re_max_rel <- list(participant = list(Prequestioned = "rel_c"),
                   sentence    = list(Prequestioned = "rel_c"))

fit_rel <- function(dv, family) {
  d <- droplevels(dat_rel[!is.na(dat_rel[[dv]]), ])
  fit_glmm(paste(dv, "~ relevance"), d, family, re_max_rel)
}

rel_models <- rel_dvs |>
  mutate(model   = map2(dv, family, fit_rel),
         re_used = map_chr(model, ~ attr(.x, "re_used")))

rel_tab <- rel_models |>
  mutate(tab = map(model, \(m) est_contrasts(m, contrast = "relevance",
                                             comparison = "revpairwise") |>
                     as.data.frame() |>
                     add_satterthwaite(m, focal = "relevance"))) |>
  select(dv, label, unit, family, directional, re_used, model, tab) |>
  unnest(tab) |>
  (\(x) mutate(x, t = if ("t" %in% names(x)) t else NA_real_,
                  z = if ("z" %in% names(x)) z else NA_real_,
                  df = if ("df" %in% names(x)) df else NA_real_))() |>
  mutate(stat_name = if_else(is.na(t), "z", "t"),
         stat = coalesce(t, z),
         df = coalesce(df, Inf),
         # one-sided (Prequestioned > Non) where a direction was preregistered (durations,
         # re-reading); two-sided for first-pass regression
         p_type = if_else(directional, "one-sided", "two-sided"),
         p_test = if_else(p_type == "one-sided", pt(stat, df, lower.tail = FALSE), p),
         n_obs = map_int(model, nobs),
         # probabilities -> percentage points
         across(c(Difference, SE, CI_low, CI_high), \(x) if_else(unit == "%", 100 * x, x)))

stopifnot(all(rel_tab$Level1 == "Prequestioned"))

rel_tab |>
  transmute(DV = label, `Random effects` = re_used, `N obs` = n_obs,
            Contrast = paste(Level1, "−", Level2), Difference, SE,
            `95% CI` = fmt_ci(CI_low, CI_high, 1),
            Test = stat_name, Statistic = stat,
            df = if_else(is.infinite(df), "—", as.character(df)),
            p = format_p(p_test, name = NULL, digits = 3), `p type` = p_type) |>
  kable(digits = 2, caption = "Prequestioned − Non-prequestioned (Polio and TB conditions only)")
```

```{r}
facet_lab <- set_names(paste0(rel_dvs$label, " (", rel_dvs$unit, ")"), rel_dvs$dv)
fct_dv <- \(x) factor(facet_lab[x], levels = facet_lab)
```

```{r}
#| label: rel-writeup-helpers
R_txt <- function(dv_name) {
  r <- filter(rel_tab, dv == dv_name)
  stopifnot(nrow(r) == 1)
  d <- switch(r$unit, ms = 0, `ms/word` = 1, `%` = 1, 2)
  unit_txt <- if (r$unit == "%") "percentage points" else r$unit
  stat_txt <- if (r$stat_name == "z") sprintf("*z* = %s", apa_num(r$stat)) else
    sprintf("*t*(%.0f) = %s", r$df, apa_num(r$stat))
  one <- r$p_type == "one-sided"
  sprintf("%s = %s %s, %s, %s, %s",
          if (r$unit == "%") "Δ" else "*b*",
          apa_num(r$Difference, d), unit_txt,
          ci_part(r$Difference, r$SE, r$CI_low, r$CI_high, one, r$df, d),
          stat_txt, p_part(r$p_test, r$stat, r$df, one))
}
# Model-estimated percentage of first-pass regressions for one relevance level
RM_txt <- function(dv_name, rel) {
  r <- filter(rel_means, dv == dv_name, relevance == rel)
  stopifnot(nrow(r) == 1)
  paste0(fmt_num(r$Mean, 1), "%")
}
R_sig <- function(dv_name) filter(rel_tab, dv == dv_name)$p_test < .05
n_rel <- n_distinct(dat_rel$participant)
```

**Results.** The analysis included the `r n_rel` participants in the two prequestion
conditions.

*Global measures.* Total gaze duration is analysed with the ex-Gaussian model below.
Prequestioned sentences were re-read with probability
`r RM_txt("reread_any", "Prequestioned")`, non-prequestioned sentences with probability
`r RM_txt("reread_any", "Non-prequestioned")`, a `r yn(R_sig("reread_any"))` difference,
`r R_txt("reread_any")`. When a sentence was re-read, the difference in re-reading
duration was `r yn(R_sig("reread_time"))`, `r R_txt("reread_time")`.

*Local measures.* The difference was `r yn(R_sig("first_pass"))` for first-pass
duration, `r R_txt("first_pass")`. The probability of a first-pass regression was
`r RM_txt("fp_regression", "Prequestioned")` for prequestioned and
`r RM_txt("fp_regression", "Non-prequestioned")` for non-prequestioned sentences, a
`r yn(R_sig("fp_regression"))` difference, `r R_txt("fp_regression")`
(@fig-relevance).

The random-effects structures selected were:
`r paste(sprintf("%s, %s", tolower(rel_tab$label), rel_tab$re_used), collapse = "; ")`.
The duration contrasts use Satterthwaite degrees of freedom.

Because total gaze duration = first-pass + second-pass time, comparing the first-pass and
second-pass contrasts shows *when* any extra processing of prequestioned sentences
happens. This comparison is descriptive. A significant contrast in one measure and a
non-significant contrast in the other does not by itself show that the two differ.


### Ex-Gaussian model of total gaze duration

::: callout-warning
## Exploratory

The preregistration specifies an ex-Gaussian model for skewed durations, with the focus
on μ, fitted in `brms`. These models use `gamlss` instead, to obtain frequentist tests,
with a simpler random-effects structure (see below), so it deviates from the
preregistered specification.
:::

Total gaze duration (`r dur_unit`) is modelled as ex-Gaussian (`gamlss`, `exGAUS`
family) with relevance predicting μ (Gaussian mean) and τ (exponential tail, log link).
σ is constant. A participant random intercept on μ (`re()`) absorbs reader
differences:

```r
gamlss(total_gaze ~ relevance + re(random = ~ 1 | participant),
       sigma.formula = ~ 1, nu.formula = ~ relevance, family = exGAUS)
```

Simplifications, all because the `gamlss` estimation failed numerically otherwise:

- The preregistered structure (relevance also on σ, and participant random effects on
  all three parameters) could not be fitted.
- Sentence is not in the model (neither as a random nor as a fixed effect). Each
  sentence is prequestioned for one condition and not for the other, so the comparison
  is balanced over sentences, but sentence variability is left in the residual.
- **First-pass and second-pass time are not modelled.** Second-pass time is 0 (the
  sentence was read only once) for
  `r round(100 * mean(dat_rel$second_pass == 0, na.rm = TRUE))`% of sentences, which an
  ex-Gaussian cannot describe, and the first-pass model did not converge (σ collapses to
  zero).

Differences are Prequestioned − Non-prequestioned in `r dur_unit`, with delta-method
standard errors, 95% Wald CIs, and one-sided *p*-values (Prequestioned >
Non-prequestioned). The overall mean is μ + τ. As in the other `gamlss` models, the
standard errors are conditional on the random-effect estimates.

```{r}
#| label: rel-exgauss-fit
rel_ex_scale <- if (length_norm) 100 else 1000
rel_ex_dvs <- c(total_fix = "Total gaze duration")

# gamlss's vcov() refits the model, looking its data up by name in the global
# environment, so each data set is stored there under its own name
fit_rel_ex <- function(dv) {
  dname <- paste0("rel_ex_", dv)
  assign(dname, envir = globalenv(),
         dat_rel |>
           filter(!is.na(.data[[dv]])) |>
           transmute(y = .data[[dv]] / rel_ex_scale, rel_c, participant,
                     sentence = factor(sentence)) |>
           as.data.frame())
  m <- eval(bquote(gamlss(y ~ rel_c + re(random = ~ 1 | participant),
                          sigma.formula = ~ 1, nu.formula = ~ rel_c,
                          family = exGAUS, data = .(as.name(dname)),
                          control = gamlss.control(n.cyc = 200, trace = FALSE))),
            envir = globalenv())
  stopifnot(m$converged)
  m
}

# Prequestioned - Non-prequestioned for mu, tau and the mean (delta method)
rel_ex_contrasts <- function(m) {
  b_mu <- coef(m, "mu"); b_mu <- b_mu[!is.na(b_mu)]
  b_nu <- coef(m, "nu")
  V <- suppressWarnings(vcov(m, type = "vcov"))
  k <- length(b_mu)
  stopifnot(nrow(V) == k + 1 + length(b_nu))
  i_mu <- which(names(b_mu) == "rel_c"); i_nu <- k + 1 + seq_along(b_nu)
  tau <- exp(b_nu[["(Intercept)"]] + c(0.5, -0.5) * b_nu[["rel_c"]])
  g_tau <- numeric(nrow(V))
  g_tau[i_nu] <- c(tau[1] - tau[2], 0.5 * (tau[1] + tau[2]))   # d(tau1 - tau2)/d(b_nu)
  g_mu <- numeric(nrow(V)); g_mu[i_mu] <- 1
  est <- c(b_mu[["rel_c"]], tau[1] - tau[2])
  tibble(parameter = c("μ (Gaussian)", "τ (tail)", "Mean"),
         pre = c(NA, tau[1], NA) * rel_ex_scale, non = c(NA, tau[2], NA) * rel_ex_scale,
         est = c(est, sum(est)),
         se = map_dbl(list(g_mu, g_tau, g_mu + g_tau), \(g) sqrt(drop(t(g) %*% V %*% g)))) |>
    mutate(across(c(est, se), \(x) x * rel_ex_scale),
           lo = est - qnorm(0.975) * se, hi = est + qnorm(0.975) * se,
           z = est / se, p = pnorm(z, lower.tail = FALSE))           # one-sided
}

rel_ex_models <- map(set_names(names(rel_ex_dvs)), fit_rel_ex)
rel_ex_tab <- imap(rel_ex_models, \(m, v) rel_ex_contrasts(m) |>
                     mutate(dv = v, label = rel_ex_dvs[[v]], n_obs = nobs(m),
                            cycles = m$iter)) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  mutate(parameter = factor(parameter, levels = c("μ (Gaussian)", "τ (tail)", "Mean")))

rel_ex_tab |>
  transmute(DV = label, Parameter = parameter, `N obs` = n_obs,
            Difference = fmt_num(est, 1), SE = fmt_num(se, 1), `95% CI` = fmt_ci(lo, hi, 1),
            z = fmt_num(z, 2), `p (one-sided)` = format_p(p, name = NULL)) |>
  kable(caption = sprintf("Ex-Gaussian Prequestioned − Non-prequestioned differences (%s), Polio and TB conditions only.",
                          dur_unit))
```

```{r}
#| label: rel-exgauss-writeup-helpers
RE_txt <- function(dv_name, par) {
  r <- filter(rel_ex_tab, dv == dv_name, parameter == par)
  stopifnot(nrow(r) == 1)
  sprintf("%s %s, %s, *z* = %s, %s", fmt_num(r$est, 1), dur_unit,
          ci_part(r$est, r$se, r$lo, r$hi, TRUE, Inf, 1), fmt_num(r$z, 2),
          p_part(r$p, r$z, Inf, TRUE))
}
```

**Results.** The model converged. Prequestioned sentences differed from
non-prequestioned sentences in the Gaussian component (μ, the preregistered focus) by
`r RE_txt("total_fix", "μ (Gaussian)")`, and in the exponential tail (τ) by
`r RE_txt("total_fix", "τ (tail)")`; the overall mean differed by
`r RE_txt("total_fix", "Mean")`.

## Global measure: second-pass regressions into the sentence (not preregistered)

::: callout-warning
## Exploratory

This measure is not preregistered. The preregistered first-pass regression measure
asks whether readers *leave* a sentence backwards during first-pass reading, which
mainly indexes difficulty integrating the sentence. The question here is the other
direction: do readers *come back* to prequestioned information from later text after
moving on (second-pass regressions, also called look-backs)?
:::

`r if (params$measures != "derived") "**This section requires the measures derived from the fixation data** (Tobii's export has no fixation sequence across sentences), so it is empty in this version of the report."`

**Measure.** A second-pass regression is a return to the sentence **from later text**,
after first-pass reading had moved past it. Re-entries from earlier text (after
regressing out of the sentence) are not counted. The DV is whether at least one
second-pass regression into the sentence occurred (0/1), for sentences read during
first-pass reading (from `derive_et_measures.R`).

**Models.** Logistic mixed models, with the Condition × Topic design used above and with
the prequestioned vs. non-prequestioned comparison (Polio and TB conditions). Random
effects are selected from the maximal structures by the same model-comparison procedure. No direction was preregistered, so all
contrasts are two-sided. Differences are in percentage points, computed from predictions
averaged over the observed sample.

```{r}
#| label: spr-models
#| eval: !expr params$measures == "derived"
# Fit the second-pass regression model. `fixed`: fixed-effects part; `re_max`: the
# maximal random-effects structure of the design (re_max_ct or re_max_rel).
fit_spr <- function(data, fixed, re_max) {
  d <- droplevels(data[!is.na(data$regressed_in), ])
  fit_glmm(paste("regressed_in ~", fixed), d, "binomial", re_max)
}

# Probabilities -> percent / percentage points
to_pct <- \(x, cols) mutate(x, across(all_of(cols), \(v) 100 * v))

# Condition x Topic design (all three conditions)
spr_model <- fit_spr(dat, "condition * topic", re_max_ct)
spr_omnibus <- as.data.frame(model_parameters(car::Anova(spr_model, type = 3))) |>
  filter(Parameter != "(Intercept)")
spr_followups <- followups(spr_model, "%") |> mutate(unit = "%")
spr_contrasts <- as.data.frame(est_contrasts(spr_model, contrast = "topic", by = "condition",
                                             comparison = "revpairwise")) |>
  to_pct(c("Difference", "SE", "CI_low", "CI_high"))
spr_means <- as.data.frame(est_means(spr_model, by = c("condition", "topic"))) |>
  rename(any_of(c(Mean = "Probability"))) |>
  to_pct(c("Mean", "CI_low", "CI_high"))

# Prequestioned vs. non-prequestioned (Polio and TB conditions)
spr_rel_model <- fit_spr(dat_rel, "relevance", re_max_rel)
spr_rel <- as.data.frame(est_contrasts(spr_rel_model, contrast = "relevance",
                                       comparison = "revpairwise")) |>
  to_pct(c("Difference", "SE", "CI_low", "CI_high"))
spr_rel_means <- as.data.frame(est_means(spr_rel_model, by = "relevance")) |>
  rename(any_of(c(Mean = "Probability"))) |>
  to_pct(c("Mean", "CI_low", "CI_high"))
stopifnot(spr_rel$Level1 == "Prequestioned")

spr_omnibus |>
  transmute(Effect = Parameter, `Wald χ²` = Chi2, df,
            p = format_p(p, name = NULL, digits = 3)) |>
  kable(digits = 2, caption = sprintf(
    "Second-pass regression, Condition × Topic: type-III Wald tests (random effects: %s)",
    attr(spr_model, "re_used")))

bind_rows(
  spr_contrasts |> transmute(Design = "Condition × Topic",
                             Comparison = paste0(condition, ": ", Level1, " − ", Level2),
                             Difference, CI_low, CI_high, z, p),
  spr_rel |> transmute(Design = "Prequestioned vs. non",
                       Comparison = paste(Level1, "−", Level2),
                       Difference, CI_low, CI_high, z, p)
) |>
  transmute(Design, Comparison, `Difference (pp)` = fmt_num(Difference, 1),
            `95% CI` = fmt_ci(CI_low, CI_high, 1), z = fmt_num(z, 2),
            `p (two-sided)` = format_p(p, name = NULL, digits = 3)) |>
  kable(caption = "Second-pass regression contrasts (percentage points)")

spr_followups |>
  transmute(Effect = effect, `Estimate (pp)` = fmt_num(estimate, 1),
            `95% CI` = fmt_ci(lo, hi, 1), z = fmt_num(stat, 2),
            p = format_p(p, name = NULL, digits = 3),
            `p (Holm)` = format_p(p_adj, name = NULL, digits = 3)) |>
  kable(caption = "Second-pass regression: main-effect and interaction contrasts (percentage points)")
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Probability of a second-pass regression into target sentences (a return from later text). Model-estimated means ± 95% CI. Left: by Condition × Topic. Right: prequestioned vs. non-prequestioned sentences (Polio and TB conditions)."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.2
p_cond <- ggplot(spr_means, aes(condition, Mean, colour = topic)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = CI_low, ymax = CI_high),
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.4), size = 0.5, linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = topic_cols, name = "Sentence topic") +
  labs(x = "Prequestion condition", y = "Sentences regressed into (%)") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```
