```{r}
                  size = 0.5, linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Sentences regressed into (%)")
p_cond + p_rel + plot_layout(widths = c(1.6, 1))
```

```{r}
#| label: spr-writeup
#| eval: !expr params$measures == "derived"
#| results: asis
SPR_txt <- function(r) {
  sprintf("Δ = %s percentage points, 95%% CI [%s, %s], *z* = %s, %s",
          fmt_num(r$Difference, 1), fmt_num(r$CI_low, 1), fmt_num(r$CI_high, 1),
          fmt_num(r$z, 2), sub("^p", "*p*", apa_p(r$p)))
}
SPR_omni <- function(term) {
  r <- filter(spr_omnibus, Parameter == term)
  sprintf("χ²(%d) = %s, %s", r$df, fmt_num(r$Chi2, 2), sub("^p", "*p*", apa_p(r$p)))
}
SPR_rel_mean <- \(rel) paste0(fmt_num(filter(spr_rel_means, relevance == rel)$Mean, 1), "%")

SPR_main <- function(term) {
  sprintf("the main effect of %s was %s, %s", term,
          yn(filter(spr_omnibus, Parameter == tolower(term))$p < .05), SPR_omni(tolower(term)))
}
cat(sprintf(paste(
  "**Results.** Readers made a second-pass regression into %s of the target sentences",
  "they had read during first-pass reading. In the Condition × Topic design, %s, %s,",
  "and the interaction was %s, %s. The Polio − TB difference was %s in the Polio condition,",
  "%s in the TB condition, and %s in Control. As for first-pass regression, topic is a",
  "property of the sentences, so these within-condition contrasts carry the",
  "between-sentence variability and have wide intervals; the interaction compares the",
  "same sentences across conditions. Comparing prequestioned with non-prequestioned",
  "sentences, readers regressed into %s of prequestioned and %s of non-prequestioned",
  "sentences, %s (@fig-spr). %s"
),
paste0(fmt_num(100 * mean(dat$regressed_in, na.rm = TRUE), 1), "%"),
SPR_main("Condition"), SPR_main("Topic"),
yn(filter(spr_omnibus, Parameter == "condition:topic")$p < .05),
SPR_omni("condition:topic"),
SPR_txt(filter(spr_contrasts, condition == "Polio")),
SPR_txt(filter(spr_contrasts, condition == "TB")),
SPR_txt(filter(spr_contrasts, condition == "Control")),
SPR_rel_mean("Prequestioned"), SPR_rel_mean("Non-prequestioned"),
SPR_txt(spr_rel),
FU_txt(spr_followups)))
```

## First-pass forward reading and re-reading (exploratory) {#sec-fp-split}

**Why.** In eye-tracking studies of text reading (e.g., Kaakinen & Hyönä, 2005), first-pass reading is often split into *forward*
fixations (on new text) and *re-reading* fixations (on text already read in the
sentence, before moving on). Lewis and Mensink (2012) found that prequestions increased
first-pass re-reading of targeted sentences but not forward reading. This section
splits first-pass reading the same way, to see which part carries the first-pass
difference. Not preregistered; all tests are two-sided.

**Measures** (`derive_et_measures.R`, Step 6b): a line-by-line copy of popEye's
`ComputeSentenceMeasures()`, applied to fixations after reading started. Forward = a
fixation on a word beyond the furthest word reached so far; re-reading = on an earlier
word (with popEye's rules for return sweeps and sentence starts). popEye's first pass
differs from first-pass duration above: it continues after a brief look back to an
earlier sentence as long as no later sentence has been entered. Durations are per word.

**Models.** Forward reading: Gamma GLMM. Re-reading, as a two-part (hurdle) model:
whether any first-pass re-reading occurred (logistic GLMM), and its duration when it did
(lognormal GLMM; the lognormal fitted these durations better than a Gamma). Each part is
fitted in the Condition × Topic design and the prequestioned vs. non-prequestioned
design, with random effects selected as for the other models.

```{r}
#| label: fp-split
#| eval: !expr params$measures == "derived"
fp_dvs <- tribble(
  ~dv,              ~label,                                     ~unit,    ~family,
  "fp_forward",     "First-pass forward reading",               dur_unit, "gamma",
  "fp_reread_any",  "First-pass re-reading: probability",        "%",      "binomial",
  "fp_reread_time", "First-pass re-reading: duration when present", dur_unit, "lognormal"
)
add_fp <- \(d) d |>
  mutate(fp_reread_any  = if_else(is.na(fp_reread), NA_integer_, as.integer(fp_reread > 0)),
         fp_reread_time = if_else(fp_reread > 0, fp_reread, NA_real_),
         fp_forward     = if_else(fp_forward > 0, fp_forward, NA_real_))
dat_fp     <- add_fp(dat)
dat_fp_rel <- add_fp(dat_rel)

fp_share_reread <- mean(dat_fp$fp_reread_any, na.rm = TRUE)

fit_fp <- function(d, fixed_rhs, re_max) {
  map2(fp_dvs$dv, fp_dvs$family, \(v, f)
       fit_glmm(paste(v, "~", fixed_rhs), droplevels(d[!is.na(d[[v]]), ]), f, re_max)) |>
    set_names(fp_dvs$dv)
}
fp_ct_models  <- fit_fp(dat_fp, "condition * topic", re_max_ct)
fp_rel_models <- fit_fp(dat_fp_rel, "relevance", re_max_rel)

# probabilities -> percent (unit is a single value per measure)
pct_if <- \(x, unit) if (unit == "%") 100 * x else x

# Prequestioned - Non-prequestioned (two-sided)
fp_rel_tab <- imap_dfr(fp_rel_models, \(m, v) {
  u <- fp_dvs$unit[fp_dvs$dv == v]
  as.data.frame(est_contrasts(m, contrast = "relevance", comparison = "revpairwise")) |>
    transmute(dv = v, Difference = pct_if(Difference, u), CI_low = pct_if(CI_low, u),
              CI_high = pct_if(CI_high, u), z, p)
})
stopifnot(all(fp_rel_tab$dv == fp_dvs$dv))
fp_rel_means <- imap_dfr(fp_rel_models, \(m, v) {
  u <- fp_dvs$unit[fp_dvs$dv == v]
  as.data.frame(est_means(m, by = "relevance")) |>
    rename(Mean = any_of(c("Mean", "Probability"))) |>
    transmute(dv = v, relevance, Mean = pct_if(Mean, u))
})

# Condition x Topic: omnibus tests and Polio - TB within each condition (two-sided)
fp_ct_omni <- imap_dfr(fp_ct_models, \(m, v) mutate(omnibus(m, "x"), dv = v))
fp_ct_con  <- imap_dfr(fp_ct_models, \(m, v) {
  u <- fp_dvs$unit[fp_dvs$dv == v]
  as.data.frame(est_contrasts(m, contrast = "topic", by = "condition",
                              comparison = "revpairwise")) |>
    transmute(dv = v, condition, Difference = pct_if(Difference, u),
              CI_low = pct_if(CI_low, u), CI_high = pct_if(CI_high, u), z, p)
})

fp_rel_tab |>
  left_join(select(fp_dvs, dv, label), by = "dv") |>
  left_join(fp_rel_means |> pivot_wider(names_from = relevance, values_from = Mean),
            by = "dv") |>
  transmute(Measure = label, Prequestioned, `Non-prequestioned`, Difference,
            `95% CI` = fmt_ci(CI_low, CI_high, 1), z,
            p = format_p(p, name = NULL, digits = 3),
            `Random effects` = map_chr(fp_rel_models, ~ attr(.x, "re_used"))) |>
  kable(digits = 1, caption = "Prequestioned vs. non-prequestioned (Polio and TB conditions): model-estimated means and differences (ms/word or %)")

fp_ct_omni |>
  filter(Parameter == "condition:topic") |>
  left_join(select(fp_dvs, dv, label), by = "dv") |>
  transmute(Measure = label, `Wald χ²` = stat, df, p = format_p(p, name = NULL, digits = 3)) |>
  kable(digits = 2, caption = "Condition × Topic interaction")

fp_ct_con |>
  left_join(select(fp_dvs, dv, label), by = "dv") |>
  transmute(Measure = label, Condition = condition, `Polio − TB` = Difference,
            `95% CI` = fmt_ci(CI_low, CI_high, 1), z,
            p = format_p(p, name = NULL, digits = 3)) |>
  kable(digits = 1, caption = "Polio − TB within each condition (two-sided)")
```

## Mediation: does reading time account for the memory benefit? (not preregistered)

::: callout-warning
## Exploratory

This analysis was not preregistered. It asks how much of the memory benefit for
prequestioned information can be explained by the extra reading time prequestioned
sentences receive.
:::

**Design.** Each of the 10 target sentences contains the answer to exactly one test
question (mapping below), so treatment, mediator and outcome can be linked sentence by
sentence. This uses the `r n_distinct(dat_rel$participant)` participants in the two
prequestion conditions:

- **Treatment (X):** relevance, meaning whether the sentence was prequestioned for this
  reader. It varies within participants: 5 prequestioned and 5 non-prequestioned
  sentences each.
- **Mediator (M):** reading time on the sentence (`r dur_unit`), centred within
  participant, so that it compares a reader's longer- and shorter-read sentences and is
  not driven by overall reading speed. The participant's mean reading time is included
  in the outcome model as a covariate.
- **Outcome (Y):** points earned on the corresponding test question (binomial, out of the
  question's points).

**Models.** Each path is a mixed model fitted with `gamlss`, with random intercepts
entered as penalised `random()` terms:

```r
# mediator (a path): reading time, Gaussian
gamlss(gaze_within ~ relevance + random(question), family = NO)
# outcome (b and c′ paths): points out of the question's maximum, binomial
gamlss(cbind(points, max - points) ~ relevance + gaze_within + gaze_between +
         random(participant) + random(question), family = BI)
```

The indirect effect (*a* × *b*), direct effect (*c*′), total effect (*a**b* + *c*′) and
proportion mediated (*a**b* / total) are point estimates from the fitted coefficients.
Their 95% CIs and two-sided *p*-values come from the Monte Carlo method (Preacher &
Selig, 2012): `r format(2e4, big.mark = ",")` draws of the *a* path from the mediator
model and of the *b* and *c*′ paths jointly from the outcome model's covariance matrix.
In the parallel model, the two *a* paths are drawn jointly, with their correlation set to
the correlation of the two mediator models' residuals. Effects are on the log-odds
scale. Relevance is coded −0.5 (non-prequestioned) / +0.5 (prequestioned), and reading
time is in units of 10 `r dur_unit`.

```{r}
#| label: med-data
q_map <- tribble(
  ~questnum, ~pattern,
  1,  "provides 17%",
  2,  "^Polio has no cure",
  3,  "Nigeria",
  4,  "Supportive measures",
  5,  "classic symptoms",
  6,  "only 10%",
  7,  "long-term course",
  8,  "not latent",
  9,  "spread through the air",
  10, "dropped from many hundreds"
)

sentence_q <- tibble(sentence = levels(dat$sentence)) |>
  mutate(questnum = map_dbl(sentence, \(s) {
    hit <- q_map$questnum[str_detect(s, q_map$pattern)]
    if (length(hit) == 1) hit else NA_real_
  }))
stopifnot(sum(!is.na(sentence_q$questnum)) == 10,
          !anyDuplicated(na.omit(sentence_q$questnum)))

answer_key <- read_csv("stimuli/answer_key.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

sentence_q |>
  filter(!is.na(questnum)) |>
  left_join(select(answer_key, questnum, Question), by = "questnum") |>
  arrange(questnum) |>
  transmute(Q = questnum, Question, Sentence = str_trunc(sentence, 70)) |>
  kable(caption = "Mapping of target sentences to test questions")

med <- dat_rel |>
  mutate(sentence = as.character(sentence), participant = as.character(participant)) |>
  left_join(mutate(sentence_q, sentence = as.character(sentence)), by = "sentence") |>
  inner_join(read_csv("data/derived/test_scored_items.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
               select(participant = et_id, questnum, q_points = points, q_max = max_points),
             by = c("participant", "questnum")) |>
  filter(!is.na(total_fix)) |>
  mutate(gaze = total_fix / 10,                          # units of 10 ms/word (or ms)
         q_fail = q_max - q_points,
         first_pass_raw = coalesce(first_pass, 0)) |>   # first-pass, 0 if skipped
  group_by(participant) |>
  mutate(gaze_between = mean(gaze), gaze_within = gaze - gaze_between) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(gaze_between = gaze_between - mean(gaze_between),
         participant = factor(participant), question = factor(questnum))

stopifnot(all(med$q_points <= med$q_max))
```


```{r}
#| label: med-helpers
n_mc <- 2e4
ctrl_med <- gamlss.control(trace = FALSE, n.cyc = 100)
# gamlss's vcov() refits the model, looking up its data by name in the global
# environment, so models are fitted on a named global data frame (`d` is its name)
fit_gamlss <- function(f, d, family) {
  eval(bquote(gamlss(.(f), data = .(as.name(d)), family = .(family), control = ctrl_med)),
       envir = globalenv())
}
fit_m <- function(f, d) fit_gamlss(f, d, quote(NO))
fit_y <- function(f, d) fit_gamlss(f, d, quote(BI))

# Fixed mu coefficients and their covariance (random() terms have no fixed coefficient)
mu_fixed <- function(m) {
  b <- coef(m, "mu")
  b <- b[!is.na(b)]
  V <- suppressWarnings(vcov(m, type = "vcov"))[seq_along(b), seq_along(b)]
  dimnames(V) <- list(names(b), names(b))
  list(b = b, V = V)
}

# Monte Carlo draws of the relevance -> mediator paths (a), one model per mediator.
# Paths are drawn jointly, correlated as the mediator models' residuals are.
a_draws <- function(ms) {
  est <- map_dbl(ms, \(m) mu_fixed(m)$b[["rel_c"]])
  se  <- map_dbl(ms, \(m) sqrt(mu_fixed(m)$V["rel_c", "rel_c"]))
  R   <- cor(sapply(ms, resid))
  dr  <- MASS::mvrnorm(n_mc, est, diag(se, length(se)) %*% R %*% diag(se, length(se)))
  list(est = est, draws = matrix(dr, ncol = length(ms), dimnames = list(NULL, names(ms))))
}

# Monte Carlo draws of the outcome-model paths (b, c′)
y_draws <- function(m, terms) {
  f <- mu_fixed(m)
  list(est = f$b[terms], draws = MASS::mvrnorm(n_mc, f$b[terms], f$V[terms, terms]))
}

summ_mc <- function(est, draws) {
  imap(est, \(e, nm) {
    x <- draws[[nm]]
    tibble(Effect = nm, est = e,
           lo = unname(quantile(x, 0.025)), hi = unname(quantile(x, 0.975)),
           p = if (str_starts(nm, "Proportion")) NA_real_
               else 2 * min(mean(x > 0), mean(x < 0)))
  }) |> bind_rows()
}

fmt_med_tab <- function(tab, caption) {
  tab |>
    mutate(prop = str_starts(Effect, "Proportion"),
           Estimate = if_else(prop, paste0(fmt_num(100 * est, 1), "%"), fmt_num(est, 3)),
           `95% CI` = if_else(prop, fmt_ci(100 * lo, 100 * hi, 1), fmt_ci(lo, hi, 3)),
           p = if_else(prop, "", format_p(p, name = NULL))) |>
    select(Effect, Estimate, `95% CI`, p) |>
    kable(caption = caption)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: med-total
set.seed(2025)
md <- med |>
  select(gaze_within, gaze_between, rel_c, q_points, q_fail, participant, question) |>
  as.data.frame()                                    # gamlss refuses NA in any column

m_a <- fit_m(gaze_within ~ rel_c + random(question), "md")
m_y <- fit_y(cbind(q_points, q_fail) ~ rel_c + gaze_within + gaze_between +
               random(participant) + random(question), "md")
stopifnot(m_a$converged, m_y$converged)

med_effects <- function(a, b, cp) list(
  `a: relevance → reading time` = a,
  `b: reading time → recall` = b,
  `c′: direct effect` = cp,
  `a × b: indirect effect` = a * b,
  `c: total effect` = a * b + cp,
  `Proportion mediated` = (a * b) / (a * b + cp)
)

A <- a_draws(list(gaze = m_a))
Y <- y_draws(m_y, c("gaze_within", "rel_c"))
med_tab <- summ_mc(med_effects(A$est[["gaze"]], Y$est[["gaze_within"]], Y$est[["rel_c"]]),
                   med_effects(A$draws[, "gaze"], Y$draws[, "gaze_within"], Y$draws[, "rel_c"]))

fmt_med_tab(med_tab, sprintf(
  "Mediation by total gaze duration (%d participants, %d sentence × question observations). a in units of 10 %s; b in log-odds per 10 %s; c, c′ and a × b in log-odds. Monte Carlo 95%% CIs.",
  n_distinct(med$participant), nrow(med), dur_unit, dur_unit))
```

```{r}
#| label: med-parallel
par_dat <- function(d) {
  d |>
    mutate(fp = first_pass_raw / 10, sp = second_pass / 10) |>
    group_by(participant) |>
    mutate(firstb = mean(fp), firstw = fp - firstb,
           secondb = mean(sp), secondw = sp - secondb) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(firstb = firstb - mean(firstb),
           secondb = secondb - mean(secondb)) |>
    select(firstw, firstb, secondw, secondb, rel_c, q_points, q_fail, participant, question) |>
    as.data.frame()
}

par_effects <- function(a1, a2, b1, b2, cp) {
  tot <- a1 * b1 + a2 * b2 + cp
  list(`a₁: relevance → first-pass` = a1, `a₂: relevance → second-pass` = a2,
       `b₁: first-pass → recall` = b1, `b₂: second-pass → recall` = b2,
       `c′: direct effect` = cp,
       `a₁b₁: indirect via first-pass` = a1 * b1, `a₂b₂: indirect via second-pass` = a2 * b2,
       `Total indirect` = a1 * b1 + a2 * b2, `a₁b₁ − a₂b₂` = a1 * b1 - a2 * b2,
       `c: total effect` = tot,
       `Proportion mediated: first-pass` = a1 * b1 / tot,
       `Proportion mediated: second-pass` = a2 * b2 / tot,
       `Proportion mediated: total` = (a1 * b1 + a2 * b2) / tot)
}

fit_parallel <- function(d) {                       # d: name of a global data frame
  m1 <- fit_m(firstw ~ rel_c + random(question), d)
  m2 <- fit_m(secondw ~ rel_c + random(question), d)
  my <- fit_y(cbind(q_points, q_fail) ~ rel_c + firstw + firstb + secondw + secondb +
                random(participant) + random(question), d)
  stopifnot(m1$converged, m2$converged, my$converged)
  A <- a_draws(list(first = m1, second = m2))
  Y <- y_draws(my, c("firstw", "secondw", "rel_c"))
  summ_mc(par_effects(A$est[["first"]], A$est[["second"]],
                      Y$est[["firstw"]], Y$est[["secondw"]], Y$est[["rel_c"]]),
          par_effects(A$draws[, "first"], A$draws[, "second"],
                      Y$draws[, "firstw"], Y$draws[, "secondw"], Y$draws[, "rel_c"]))
}

set.seed(2025)
d_all <- par_dat(med)
d_fp  <- par_dat(filter(med, first_pass_raw > 0))
par_all <- fit_parallel("d_all")
par_fp  <- fit_parallel("d_fp")

bind_rows(`All sentences` = par_all, `First-pass > 0 only` = par_fp, .id = "Sample") |>
  mutate(prop = str_starts(Effect, "Proportion"),
         est = if_else(prop, paste0(fmt_num(100 * est, 1), "%"), fmt_num(est, 3)),
         ci = if_else(prop, fmt_ci(100 * lo, 100 * hi, 1), fmt_ci(lo, hi, 3)),
         p = if_else(prop, "", format_p(p, name = NULL))) |>
  select(Sample, Effect, est, ci, p) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Sample, values_from = c(est, ci, p), names_glue = "{Sample}: {.value}") |>
  select(Effect, starts_with("All"), starts_with("First")) |>
  rename_with(\(x) str_replace(x, ": est$", ": estimate") |> str_replace(": ci$", ": 95% CI")) |>
  kable(caption = sprintf(
    "Parallel mediation by first-pass and second-pass time. All sentences: %d observations; first-pass > 0: %d observations. Monte Carlo 95%% CIs.",
    nrow(d_all), nrow(d_fp)))
```

```{r}
#| label: med-tail
# LONG READINGS AS THE MEDIATOR (exploratory)
# The ex-Gaussian analysis located the prequestion effect on total gaze in the tail of
# unusually long readings (τ). τ describes a distribution, not a single reading, so the
# sentence-level counterpart is used here: was this reading unusually long for this
# reader? A reading is "long" if its total gaze duration (per word) is above the
# reader's own q-th percentile, computed over ALL sentences the reader fixated (target
# and filler sentences on all four pages), so the prequestioned sentences do not set
# their own cutoff. Thresholds: 70th, 80th (main) and 90th percentiles.
#
# Paths:
#   a  = change in the probability of a long reading (prequestioned - non-prequestioned),
#        from a logistic model with participant and question random intercepts
#   b  = effect of a long reading on recall (log-odds), within readers: the outcome
#        model includes the reader's rate of long readings as a covariate
#   indirect = b * a: the expected shift in the log-odds of recall produced by the
#        change in long readings, on the same scale as the direct effect c′
tail_thresholds <- c(`70th` = 0.7, `80th` = 0.8, `90th` = 0.9)

reader_gaze <- measures_src |>
  filter(participant %in% unique(med$participant), total > 0) |>
  mutate(gaze_all = if (length_norm) total / number_of_units else total) |>
  select(participant, gaze_all)

tail_effects <- function(a, b, cp) list(
  `a: relevance → long reading (probability)` = a,
  `b: long reading → recall` = b,
  `c′: direct effect` = cp,
  `a × b: indirect effect` = a * b,
  `c: total effect` = a * b + cp,
  `Proportion mediated` = (a * b) / (a * b + cp)
)

fit_tail <- function(q, label) {
  cutoffs <- reader_gaze |>
    group_by(participant) |>
    summarise(cutoff = quantile(gaze_all, q), .groups = "drop")
  dname <- paste0("md_tail_", label)
  d <- med |>
    left_join(cutoffs, by = c(participant = "participant")) |>
    mutate(long = as.integer(total_fix > cutoff)) |>
    group_by(participant) |>
    mutate(long_rate = mean(long)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(long_rate = long_rate - mean(long_rate),
           participant = factor(participant)) |>          # random() needs factors
    select(long, long_rate, rel_c, q_points, q_fail, participant, question) |>
    as.data.frame()
  stopifnot(!anyNA(d))
  assign(dname, d, envir = globalenv())     # gamlss's vcov() looks the data up by name

  m_long <- fit_gamlss(long ~ rel_c + random(participant) + random(question), dname,
                       quote(BI))
  m_rec  <- fit_gamlss(cbind(q_points, q_fail) ~ rel_c + long + long_rate +
                         random(participant) + random(question), dname, quote(BI))
  stopifnot(m_long$converged, m_rec$converged)

  # a: probability scale, at the average participant and question
  fa <- mu_fixed(m_long)
  a_dr <- MASS::mvrnorm(n_mc, fa$b[c("(Intercept)", "rel_c")],
                        fa$V[c("(Intercept)", "rel_c"), c("(Intercept)", "rel_c")])
  dp <- \(b0, b1) plogis(b0 + 0.5 * b1) - plogis(b0 - 0.5 * b1)
  a_est <- dp(fa$b[["(Intercept)"]], fa$b[["rel_c"]])
  a_draw <- dp(a_dr[, 1], a_dr[, 2])
  Y <- y_draws(m_rec, c("long", "rel_c"))

  summ_mc(tail_effects(a_est, Y$est[["long"]], Y$est[["rel_c"]]),
          tail_effects(a_draw, Y$draws[, "long"], Y$draws[, "rel_c"])) |>
    mutate(threshold = label, share_long = mean(d$long),
           long_pre = mean(d$long[d$rel_c > 0]), long_non = mean(d$long[d$rel_c < 0]))
}

set.seed(2025)
tail_tab <- imap(tail_thresholds, fit_tail) |> bind_rows()

tail_tab |>
  mutate(prop = str_starts(Effect, "Proportion"),
         est_txt = case_when(prop ~ paste0(fmt_num(100 * est, 1), "%"),
                             str_starts(Effect, "a:") ~ fmt_num(100 * est, 1),
                             TRUE ~ fmt_num(est, 3)),
         ci_txt = case_when(prop ~ fmt_ci(100 * lo, 100 * hi, 1),
                            str_starts(Effect, "a:") ~ fmt_ci(100 * lo, 100 * hi, 1),
                            TRUE ~ fmt_ci(lo, hi, 3)),
         p_txt = if_else(prop, "", format_p(p, name = NULL))) |>
  select(threshold, Effect, est_txt, ci_txt, p_txt) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = threshold, values_from = c(est_txt, ci_txt, p_txt),
              names_glue = "{threshold}: {.value}") |>
  select(Effect, starts_with("70th"), starts_with("80th"), starts_with("90th")) |>
  rename_with(\(x) x |> str_replace(": est_txt", ": estimate") |>
                str_replace(": ci_txt", ": 95% CI") |> str_replace(": p_txt", ": p")) |>
  kable(caption = "Mediation by long readings (reading above the reader's own 70th, 80th or 90th percentile of total gaze). a in percentage points (change in the probability of a long reading); b in log-odds per long reading; c, c′ and a × b in log-odds. Monte Carlo 95% CIs.")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-path
#| fig-cap: "Path models of the prequestion memory benefit (estimates with Monte Carlo 95% CIs; log-odds scale for paths into recall). A: total gaze duration as mediator. B: first-pass and second-pass time as parallel mediators (all sentences). Reading-time paths are in units of 10 ms/word (or ms)."
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.6
lab <- function(tab, eff, d = 2) {
  r <- filter(tab, Effect == eff)
  sprintf("%s\n[%s, %s]", fmt_num(r$est, d), fmt_num(r$lo, d), fmt_num(r$hi, d))
}
pct <- function(tab, eff) {
  r <- filter(tab, Effect == eff)
  sprintf("%s%% [%s, %s]", fmt_num(100 * r$est, 1), fmt_num(100 * r$lo, 1),
          fmt_num(100 * r$hi, 1))
}

path_plot <- function(nodes, edges, title, subtitle) {
  ggplot() +
    geom_segment(data = edges,
                 aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend),
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.25, "cm"), type = "closed"),
                 linewidth = 0.7, colour = "grey30") +
    geom_label(data = edges, aes(x = (x + xend) / 2 + lx, y = (y + yend) / 2 + ly, label = label),
               size = 3.1, linewidth = 0, fill = "white", lineheight = 0.9) +
    geom_label(data = nodes, aes(x, y, label = label), size = 3.5, fontface = "bold",
               label.padding = unit(0.45, "lines"), fill = "grey95", lineheight = 0.9) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-0.35, 2.35), ylim = c(-0.45, 1.35)) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle) +
    theme_void(base_size = 11) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9.5))
}

# trim arrow ends so they stop at the node boxes
trim <- function(e, k = 0.22) {
  dx <- e$xend - e$x; dy <- e$yend - e$y; len <- sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2)
  mutate(e, x = x + k * dx / len, y = y + k * dy / len,
         xend = xend - k * dx / len, yend = yend - k * dy / len)
}

pA <- path_plot(
  nodes = tibble(x = c(0, 1, 2), y = c(0, 1, 0),
                 label = c("Prequestioned\n(vs. non)", "Gaze duration\n(within reader)", "Recall of\nanswer")),
  edges = trim(tibble(x = c(0, 1, 0), y = c(0, 1, 0), xend = c(1, 2, 2), yend = c(1, 0, 0),
                      lx = c(-0.22, 0.22, 0), ly = c(0.08, 0.08, -0.16),
                      label = c(paste0("a = ", lab(med_tab, "a: relevance → reading time")),
                                paste0("b = ", lab(med_tab, "b: reading time → recall", 3)),
                                paste0("c′ = ", lab(med_tab, "c′: direct effect"))))),
  title = "A. Total gaze duration",
  subtitle = sprintf("Indirect a × b = %s; proportion mediated = %s",
                     sub("\n", " ", lab(med_tab, "a × b: indirect effect", 3)),
                     pct(med_tab, "Proportion mediated")))

pB <- path_plot(
  nodes = tibble(x = c(0, 1, 1, 2), y = c(0.5, 1.15, -0.15, 0.5),
                 label = c("Prequestioned\n(vs. non)", "First-pass\ntime", "Second-pass\ntime",
                           "Recall of\nanswer")),
  edges = trim(tibble(x = c(0, 1, 0, 1, 0), y = c(0.5, 1.15, 0.5, -0.15, 0.5),
                      xend = c(1, 2, 1, 2, 2), yend = c(1.15, 0.5, -0.15, 0.5, 0.5),
                      lx = c(-0.24, 0.24, -0.24, 0.24, 0), ly = c(0.1, 0.1, -0.1, -0.1, 0.12),
                      label = c(paste0("a₁ = ", lab(par_all, "a₁: relevance → first-pass")),
                                paste0("b₁ = ", lab(par_all, "b₁: first-pass → recall", 3)),
                                paste0("a₂ = ", lab(par_all, "a₂: relevance → second-pass")),
                                paste0("b₂ = ", lab(par_all, "b₂: second-pass → recall", 3)),
                                paste0("c′ = ", lab(par_all, "c′: direct effect"))))),
  title = "B. First-pass and second-pass time",
  subtitle = sprintf("Indirect via first-pass = %s; via second-pass = %s",
                     pct(par_all, "Proportion mediated: first-pass"),
                     pct(par_all, "Proportion mediated: second-pass")))

pA + pB
```

```{r}
#| label: med-writeup
B_row <- function(tab, eff) filter(tab, Effect == eff)
B_txt <- function(tab, eff, d = 3) {
  r <- B_row(tab, eff)
  sprintf("%s, 95%% CI [%s, %s], %s", fmt_num(r$est, d), fmt_num(r$lo, d),
          fmt_num(r$hi, d), format_p(r$p))
}
B_pct <- function(tab, eff) {
  r <- B_row(tab, eff)
  sprintf("%s%% (95%% CI [%s%%, %s%%])", fmt_num(100 * r$est, 1),
          fmt_num(100 * r$lo, 1), fmt_num(100 * r$hi, 1))
}
B_or <- function(tab, eff) {
  r <- B_row(tab, eff)
  sprintf("OR = %s [%s, %s]", fmt_num(exp(r$est)), fmt_num(exp(r$lo)), fmt_num(exp(r$hi)))
}
```

**Results: total gaze duration.** Prequestioned sentences were read longer than
non-prequestioned sentences (*a* = `r B_txt(med_tab, "a: relevance → reading time", 2)`,
units of 10 `r dur_unit`). Within readers, longer reading of a sentence predicted better
recall of its answer (*b* = `r B_txt(med_tab, "b: reading time → recall")`). The
indirect effect was *a* × *b* = `r B_txt(med_tab, "a × b: indirect effect")`, the
direct effect was *c*′ = `r B_txt(med_tab, "c′: direct effect")`
(`r B_or(med_tab, "c′: direct effect")`), and the total effect was
*c* = `r B_txt(med_tab, "c: total effect")` (`r B_or(med_tab, "c: total effect")`).
Reading time accounted for `r B_pct(med_tab, "Proportion mediated")` of the memory
benefit (@fig-path A).

**Results: first-pass and second-pass time.** With all sentences, the indirect effect was
`r B_txt(par_all, "a₁b₁: indirect via first-pass")` via first-pass time and
`r B_txt(par_all, "a₂b₂: indirect via second-pass")` via second-pass time. Together they
accounted for `r B_pct(par_all, "Proportion mediated: total")` of the benefit
(first-pass: `r B_pct(par_all, "Proportion mediated: first-pass")`; second-pass:
`r B_pct(par_all, "Proportion mediated: second-pass")`; @fig-path B). Restricted to
sentences with first-pass time > 0, the indirect effects were
`r B_txt(par_fp, "a₁b₁: indirect via first-pass")` (first-pass) and
`r B_txt(par_fp, "a₂b₂: indirect via second-pass")` (second-pass), together
`r B_pct(par_fp, "Proportion mediated: total")`.

**Results: long readings.** Using each reader's own 80th percentile of total gaze as the
cutoff, `r fmt_num(100 * filter(tail_tab, threshold == "80th")$long_pre[1], 1)`% of
prequestioned and `r fmt_num(100 * filter(tail_tab, threshold == "80th")$long_non[1], 1)`%
of non-prequestioned target sentences received a long reading. The indirect effect via
long readings was `r B_txt(filter(tail_tab, threshold == "80th"), "a × b: indirect effect")`,
accounting for `r B_pct(filter(tail_tab, threshold == "80th"), "Proportion mediated")` of the
benefit (70th percentile: `r B_pct(filter(tail_tab, threshold == "70th"), "Proportion mediated")`;
90th percentile: `r B_pct(filter(tail_tab, threshold == "90th"), "Proportion mediated")`).

Total gaze is the sum of first-pass and second-pass time, so it is never entered in the
same model as either component. Reading time was observed, not manipulated, so the
indirect effects are correlational. Readers may also look longer at sentences they would
remember well for other reasons.

::: callout-important
First-pass time is 0 (no first pass) for `r round(100 * mean(med$first_pass_raw == 0))`%
of these sentences. `r if (params$measures == "derived") "With the derived measures these are sentences skipped during first-pass reading." else "With Tobii's metrics this is mostly the page-landing problem: Tobii treats sentences above the landing point as already passed."`
The all-sentences analysis keeps the decomposition exact (total = first-pass +
second-pass), counting first-pass as 0 for those sentences. The first-pass > 0 analysis
leaves them out.
:::

## Reading benefit and memory benefit (not preregistered)

::: callout-warning
## Exploratory

This analysis was not preregistered. It asks whether participants who directed more
reading to prequestioned content also showed a larger memory benefit for prequestioned
content.
:::

**Approach.** For each participant in the two prequestion conditions:

- **Reading benefit** = mean total gaze duration on prequestioned sentences − mean total
  gaze duration on non-prequestioned sentences
  (`r if (length_norm) "ms/word" else "ms"`).
- **Memory benefit** = proportion of points earned on prequestioned questions −
  proportion earned on non-prequestioned questions.

Each participant is compared with themselves, so general reading speed and ability cancel
out. In the Polio condition the prequestioned topic is Polio, and in the TB condition it
is TB. Because the topics differ in difficulty and sentence length, the correlation
between the two benefits is a **partial correlation controlling for condition**
(`correlation`, easystats). Pearson is the main estimate and Spearman a robustness check.
Correlations within each condition are also reported. Each benefit score rests on 5
sentences and 5 questions per topic, so the scores are noisy, and a modest true
correlation may not reach significance.

```{r}
#| label: diff-data
test_items <- read_csv("data/derived/test_scored_items.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(et_id %in% levels(dat$participant))

gaze_rel <- dat_rel |>
  group_by(participant, condition, relevance) |>
  summarise(gaze = mean(total_fix, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(participant = as.character(participant))

acc_rel <- test_items |>
  filter(et_group != "Control") |>
  mutate(condition = recode(et_group, Po = "Polio"),
         relevance = if_else(topic == condition, "Prequestioned", "Non-prequestioned")) |>
  group_by(participant = et_id, relevance) |>
  summarise(acc = sum(points) / sum(max_points), .groups = "drop")

benefit <- inner_join(gaze_rel, mutate(acc_rel, relevance = factor(relevance, levels(gaze_rel$relevance))),
                      by = c("participant", "relevance")) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = relevance, values_from = c(gaze, acc)) |>
  transmute(participant, condition = droplevels(condition),
            gaze_benefit = gaze_Prequestioned - `gaze_Non-prequestioned`,
            acc_benefit  = acc_Prequestioned - `acc_Non-prequestioned`,
            cond_TB = as.numeric(condition == "TB"))

stopifnot(nrow(benefit) == n_distinct(dat_rel$participant), !anyNA(benefit))

benefit |>
  group_by(Condition = condition) |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            `Reading benefit M (SD)` = sprintf("%s (%s)", fmt_num(mean(gaze_benefit), 1),
                                               fmt_num(sd(gaze_benefit), 1)),
            `Memory benefit M (SD)` = sprintf("%s (%s)", fmt_num(mean(acc_benefit)),
                                              fmt_num(sd(acc_benefit)))) |>
  kable(caption = sprintf("Reading benefit (%s) and memory benefit (proportion of points), prequestioned − non-prequestioned",
                          if (length_norm) "ms/word" else "ms"))
```

```{r}
#| label: diff-corr
# Partial correlation controlling for condition: the t test of reading benefit in
# lm(memory benefit ~ reading benefit + condition), converted to r (df = n - 3).
# Spearman version: the same on ranks.
part_cor <- function(method) {
  d <- benefit
  if (method == "spearman") d <- mutate(d, across(c(gaze_benefit, acc_benefit), rank))
  mp <- model_parameters(lm(acc_benefit ~ gaze_benefit + condition, data = d)) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    filter(Parameter == "gaze_benefit")
  rr <- as.data.frame(t_to_r(mp$t, mp$df_error, ci = 0.95, alternative = "two.sided"))
  tibble(r = rr$r, CI_low = rr$CI_low, CI_high = rr$CI_high, df_error = mp$df_error, p = mp$p)
}
cond_cor <- function(cnd) {
  correlation(filter(benefit, condition == cnd) |> select(gaze_benefit, acc_benefit),
              p_adjust = "none") |>
    as.data.frame()
}

pc_pear  <- part_cor("pearson")
pc_spear <- part_cor("spearman")
cc <- map(set_names(levels(benefit$condition)), cond_cor)

diff_tab <- bind_rows(
  tibble(Analysis = "Partial r (controlling for condition)", n = nrow(benefit),
         r = pc_pear$r, lo = pc_pear$CI_low, hi = pc_pear$CI_high, df = pc_pear$df_error,
         p = pc_pear$p),
  tibble(Analysis = "Partial Spearman ρ (controlling for condition)", n = nrow(benefit),
         r = pc_spear$r, lo = pc_spear$CI_low, hi = pc_spear$CI_high,
         df = pc_spear$df_error, p = pc_spear$p),
  imap(cc, \(x, cnd) tibble(Analysis = paste("Pearson r, Polio condition" |>
                                               sub("Polio", cnd, x = _)),
                            n = sum(benefit$condition == cnd), r = x$r, lo = x$CI_low,
                            hi = x$CI_high, df = x$df_error, p = x$p)) |>
    bind_rows()
)

diff_tab |>
  transmute(Analysis, n, r = fmt_num(r), `95% CI` = fmt_ci(lo, hi), df,
            p = format_p(p, name = NULL, digits = 3)) |>
  kable(caption = "Correlation between reading benefit and memory benefit")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-benefit
#| fig-cap: "Exploratory: each participant's reading benefit (gaze on prequestioned − non-prequestioned sentences) and memory benefit (accuracy on prequestioned − non-prequestioned questions), centred within condition. The line is a least-squares fit with 95% CI."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.8
cond_cols <- topic_cols

benefit |>
  group_by(condition) |>
  mutate(across(c(gaze_benefit, acc_benefit), ~ .x - mean(.x), .names = "{.col}_c")) |>
  ungroup() |>
  ggplot(aes(gaze_benefit_c, acc_benefit_c)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey85") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey85") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, colour = "grey20", fill = "grey70",
              linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = condition), size = 2, alpha = 0.75) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cond_cols, name = "Prequestion condition") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(x = sprintf("Reading benefit, centred within condition (%s)",
                   if (length_norm) "ms/word" else "ms"),
       y = "Memory benefit, centred within condition\n(percentage points)") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

```{r}
#| label: diff-writeup-helpers
fmt_r <- function(x) sub("^(-?)0\\.", "\\1.", fmt_num(x))
D_row <- function(a) filter(diff_tab, Analysis == a)
D_txt <- function(a, sym = "*r*") {
  r <- D_row(a)
  sprintf("%s(%d) = %s, 95%% CI [%s, %s], %s", sym, r$df, fmt_r(r$r), fmt_r(r$lo),
          fmt_r(r$hi), sub("^p", "*p*", apa_p(r$p)))
}
D_sig <- function(a) D_row(a)$p < .05
pc_lab <- "Partial r (controlling for condition)"
```

**Results.** On average, participants in the prequestion conditions read prequestioned
sentences longer (mean reading benefit =
`r fmt_num(mean(benefit$gaze_benefit), 1)` `r if (length_norm) "ms/word" else "ms"`) and
scored higher on prequestioned questions (mean memory benefit =
`r fmt_num(100 * mean(benefit$acc_benefit), 1)` percentage points). Across the
`r nrow(benefit)` participants, the reading benefit and the memory benefit were
`r yn(D_sig(pc_lab), "significantly", "not significantly")` correlated, controlling
for condition, `r D_txt(pc_lab)`; partial Spearman
`r D_txt("Partial Spearman ρ (controlling for condition)", "ρ")`. Within conditions,
the correlation was `r D_txt("Pearson r, Polio condition")` in the Polio condition and
`r D_txt("Pearson r, TB condition")` in the TB condition (@fig-benefit).

### Gaze and accuracy for prequestioned and non-prequestioned content

These correlations are computed separately for prequestioned content (gaze on
prequestioned sentences vs. accuracy on prequestioned questions) and non-prequestioned
content, in the same `r nrow(benefit)` participants. Each is a partial correlation
controlling for condition. The two correlations come from the same participants and share
no variable, so they are compared with a test for dependent, non-overlapping
correlations (Steiger, 1980; `cocor`) on scores centred within condition, with a 95% CI
for the difference (Zou, 2007).

```{r}
#| label: prenon-corr
library(cocor)

relcor <- inner_join(gaze_rel,
                     mutate(acc_rel, relevance = factor(relevance, levels(gaze_rel$relevance))),
                     by = c("participant", "relevance")) |>
  mutate(relevance = droplevels(relevance), condition = droplevels(condition))

# Partial r controlling for condition (as in part_cor above)
rel_part_cor <- function(rel, method = "pearson") {
  d <- filter(relcor, relevance == rel)
  if (method == "spearman") d <- mutate(d, across(c(gaze, acc), rank))
  mp <- model_parameters(lm(acc ~ gaze + condition, data = d)) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    filter(Parameter == "gaze")
  rr <- as.data.frame(t_to_r(mp$t, mp$df_error, ci = 0.95, alternative = "two.sided"))
  tibble(relevance = rel, n = nrow(d), r = rr$r, lo = rr$CI_low, hi = rr$CI_high,
         df = mp$df_error, p = mp$p)
}

prenon_tab <- bind_rows(
  map(c("Prequestioned", "Non-prequestioned"), rel_part_cor) |> bind_rows() |>
    mutate(method = "Pearson"),
  map(c("Prequestioned", "Non-prequestioned"), rel_part_cor, method = "spearman") |>
    bind_rows() |> mutate(method = "Spearman")
)

# Difference between the two correlations, on scores centred within condition
centred <- relcor |>
  group_by(condition, relevance) |>
  mutate(across(c(gaze, acc), ~ .x - mean(.x))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = participant, names_from = relevance, values_from = c(gaze, acc))
R <- cor(select(centred, gaze_Prequestioned, acc_Prequestioned,
                `gaze_Non-prequestioned`, `acc_Non-prequestioned`))
cmp <- cocor.dep.groups.nonoverlap(
  r.jk = R["gaze_Prequestioned", "acc_Prequestioned"],
  r.hm = R["gaze_Non-prequestioned", "acc_Non-prequestioned"],
  r.jh = R["gaze_Prequestioned", "gaze_Non-prequestioned"],
  r.jm = R["gaze_Prequestioned", "acc_Non-prequestioned"],
  r.kh = R["acc_Prequestioned", "gaze_Non-prequestioned"],
  r.km = R["acc_Prequestioned", "acc_Non-prequestioned"],
  n = nrow(centred), test = c("steiger1980", "zou2007"))
prenon_diff <- tibble(diff = R["gaze_Prequestioned", "acc_Prequestioned"] -
                        R["gaze_Non-prequestioned", "acc_Non-prequestioned"],
                      lo = cmp@zou2007$conf.int[1], hi = cmp@zou2007$conf.int[2],
                      z = cmp@steiger1980$statistic, p = cmp@steiger1980$p.value)

prenon_tab |>
  transmute(Content = relevance, Method = method, n, r = fmt_num(r),
            `95% CI` = fmt_ci(lo, hi), df, p = format_p(p, name = NULL, digits = 3)) |>
  kable(caption = "Partial correlations (controlling for condition) between gaze duration and test accuracy")
```

```{r}
#| label: prenon-plot-helper
plot_relcor <- function(rel) {
  relcor |>
    filter(relevance == rel) |>
    ggplot(aes(gaze, acc)) +
    geom_smooth(aes(colour = condition, fill = condition), method = "lm",
                formula = y ~ x, alpha = 0.12, linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = condition), size = 2, alpha = 0.75) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = cond_cols, name = "Prequestion condition") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = cond_cols, name = "Prequestion condition") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1), limits = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(x = sprintf("Mean total gaze duration on %s sentences (%s)", tolower(rel),
                     if (length_norm) "ms/word" else "ms"),
         y = sprintf("Accuracy on %s questions", tolower(rel))) +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-pre-corr
#| fig-cap: "Exploratory: gaze duration on prequestioned sentences and accuracy on prequestioned questions (Polio and TB conditions). Lines are least-squares fits with 95% CIs, by condition."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.8
plot_relcor("Prequestioned")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-non-corr
#| fig-cap: "Exploratory: gaze duration on non-prequestioned sentences and accuracy on non-prequestioned questions (Polio and TB conditions). Lines are least-squares fits with 95% CIs, by condition."
#| fig-width: 7
```

```{r}
#| label: prenon-writeup-helpers
PN_txt <- function(rel, method = "Pearson", sym = "*r*") {
  r <- filter(prenon_tab, relevance == rel, method == !!method)
  sprintf("%s(%d) = %s, 95%% CI [%s, %s], %s", sym, r$df, fmt_r(r$r), fmt_r(r$lo),
          fmt_r(r$hi), sub("^p", "*p*", apa_p(r$p)))
}
PN_sig <- function(rel) filter(prenon_tab, relevance == rel, method == "Pearson")$p < .05
```

**Results.** Controlling for condition, gaze duration and accuracy were
`r yn(PN_sig("Prequestioned"), "significantly", "not significantly")` correlated for
prequestioned content, `r PN_txt("Prequestioned")` (Spearman
`r PN_txt("Prequestioned", "Spearman", "ρ")`; @fig-pre-corr), and
`r yn(PN_sig("Non-prequestioned"), "significantly", "not significantly")` correlated
for non-prequestioned content, `r PN_txt("Non-prequestioned")` (Spearman
`r PN_txt("Non-prequestioned", "Spearman", "ρ")`; @fig-non-corr). The two correlations
`r if (prenon_diff$p < .05) "differed significantly" else "did not differ significantly"`,
Δ*r* = `r fmt_r(prenon_diff$diff)`, 95% CI [`r fmt_r(prenon_diff$lo)`,
`r fmt_r(prenon_diff$hi)`], *z* = `r apa_num(prenon_diff$z)`,
`r sub("^p", "*p*", apa_p(prenon_diff$p))`.

These are between-participant correlations, so they also reflect general reading speed
and skill. The reading-benefit analysis above removes those by comparing each
participant with themselves.

## Random-effects selection {#sec-re-selection}

Every comparison made by the random-effects selection procedure (see Models), for every
eye-movement GLMM (the final-test models are in `final_test.qmd`). *χ²*, *df* and *p* are from the likelihood-ratio test of the model without the
slope against the model with it.

```{r}
#| label: re-selection
glmm_list_et <- c(
  set_names(models$model, paste("Condition × Topic:", models$label)),
  set_names(rel_models$model, paste("Prequestioned vs. non:", rel_models$label)),
  if (exists("spr_model")) list(`Condition × Topic: Second-pass regression` = spr_model,
                                `Prequestioned vs. non: Second-pass regression` = spr_rel_model))
re_tabs_et <- re_selection_tables(glmm_list_et)
show_re_selection(re_tabs_et)
```
